P0B00.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase U Current
P0B00.description: P0B00 is the general fault for phase U of the three-phase motor that drives the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump, the pump that keeps line pressure while the engine is stopped. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM, which runs such pumps on the Volt, ELR, Spark EV and CT6, monitors phase U instead with the low-side code P0B01 and catches overcurrent on any phase with P0C28. A Hitachi patent for an idle-stop sub-oil pump shows that the inverter often derives every phase current from one DC-bus shunt, so a U fault may come from the shared sensor rather than the phase itself. Expect a warning lamp, a stopped pump and, depending on design, no engine auto-stop or a no-start. P0B01/P0B02 are the low and high variants, P0B03 and P0B06 phases V and W.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or unlatched phase U connection at the pump motor
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty (shunt or phase sensor)
Power stage of phase U in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase U of the pump motor

symptoms: MIL or hybrid/transmission warning message
Engine auto-stop disabled or no electric drive mode
Delayed engagement or harsh restart after a stop

P0B01.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase U Current Low
P0B01.description: P0B01 means the pump inverter sees almost no current in phase U of the auxiliary fluid pump motor, typically an open phase. GM documents the check for the Volt motor control processor (2016) and its hybrid tables of 2018 and 2019: with the drive state in Run, the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V and a squared current command above 5 A2 (2016) or 14.97 A2 (2018), the peak current on the U axis is compared while the rotor is within 30 degrees of it; below 1 A for 0.4 s of a 0.6 s window, the code sets as Type A, MIL on the first trip. On the 2014-15 Chevrolet Spark EV, GM bulletin PI1433 links P0B01, P0B04 or P0B07, Service Vehicle Soon and reduced propulsion to an unlatched pump connector. P0B04/P0B07 are phases V and W, P0B02 the high side.

causes.label: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase U lead or terminal of the pump motor cable
Phase U switch in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase U in the pump motor

symptoms: Service Vehicle Soon light and MIL
Propulsion Power Reduced or Vehicle Speed Limited message

P0B02.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase U Current High
P0B02.description: P0B02 reports excessive current in phase U of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor, an overcurrent condition that the pump inverter must cut off to protect its switches. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM handles the same case differently: on the Volt and later hybrids it sets P0C28 when the absolute current of any phase exceeds 35 A for a few milliseconds, Type A. A phase-specific high code therefore points to a shorted U lead, a shorted winding, a jammed pump or a U current sensor reading too high. The Hitachi idle-stop pump patent shows phase currents being reconstructed from one bus shunt, which makes a sensing error a real candidate. The pump usually stops; auto-stop or electric driving is blocked. P0B01 is the low side, P0B05 and P0B08 the same fault on V and W.

causes.label: Phase U lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump binding mechanically, raising motor current
Current sensing in the pump inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in phase U of the pump motor

symptoms: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump shuts down, auto-stop disabled
Harsh or delayed engagement after an engine stop

P0B03.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase V Current
P0B03.description: P0B03 covers a general current fault in phase V of the brushless motor of the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump. No manufacturer publicly describes a monitor for it. GM's 2013 eAssist (BAS Plus) tables name P0B03 only once, as a code that must be inactive before another speed check runs, without a description of its own. In GM's Volt and CT6 tables phase V is watched by the low-side code P0B04, and any overcurrent goes to P0C28. A GM, BMW and Daimler patent on a hybrid transmission pump explains why the pump matters: it must hold transmission pressure when the engine is stopped, otherwise gear engagement can be lost. The general code is a catch-all for implausible V current that fits neither low nor high. P0B04/P0B05 are the low and high variants, P0B00 and P0B06 phases U and W.

causes.label: Poor contact in the phase V lead or pump connector
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Phase V power stage in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase V of the pump motor

symptoms: MIL or transmission/hybrid warning
Engine auto-stop or electric mode no longer available

P0B04.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase V Current Low
P0B04.description: P0B04 indicates that phase V of the auxiliary fluid pump motor carries too little current, usually because the phase is open somewhere between inverter and winding. GM tests it on the Volt (2016) and in the 2018 and 2019 hybrid tables like its U and W siblings: in Run, with normal PWM, more than 50 V on the inverter and a minimum squared current command, the V current is sampled while the rotor sits within 30 degrees of the V axis. Under 1 A for 0.4 s out of 0.6 s (0.08 s windows in 2019) sets a Type A fault. GM bulletin PI1433 for the 2014-15 Spark EV names P0B04 with Service Vehicle Soon and reduced propulsion and points to the pump connector not being latched. P0B01 and P0B07 are phases U and W, P0B05 the high side, P0B03 the general V code.

causes.label: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase V lead or terminal
Phase V switch in the pump inverter not conducting
Open winding of phase V in the pump motor

symptoms: Service Vehicle Soon light and MIL
Reduced propulsion power or limited vehicle speed

P0B05.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase V Current High
P0B05.description: P0B05 flags overcurrent in phase V of the electric auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor. No manufacturer publicly documents this specific code. GM monitors the same physical fault without naming the phase: P0C28 trips when any of U, V or W exceeds 35 A for about 10 ms within a 62 ms window, and a 2018 Cadillac CT6 plug-in service update shows how a faulty pump restart routine alone can push the current over that limit. Likely triggers for a V-specific high code are a short in the V lead, shorted turns, a seized or contaminated pump, or a restart against a stalled rotor. The Hitachi patent on sub-oil pump drives shows the phase currents come from a shared sensor. Auto-stop is usually blocked. P0B04 is the low side, P0B02 and P0B08 phases U and W.

causes.label: Phase V lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump seized or contaminated, motor draws excess current
Pump restart logic in the inverter software causing overcurrent
Shorted turns in phase V of the pump motor

symptoms: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Loss of propulsion or no-start in severe cases

P0B06.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase W Current
P0B06.description: P0B06 is the general current fault for phase W of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor. No manufacturer publishes a monitor description for this exact code. GM covers phase W in its Volt, ELR and CT6 calibrations with the low-side code P0B07 and treats overcurrent on any phase as P0C28. CARB requires hybrid and transmission components whose failure affects emissions or other monitors to be checked for circuit faults and rationality, which is why manufacturers can use the general code for implausible readings. The Hitachi sub-oil pump patent describes a sinusoidal drive whose W current is calculated from a single bus shunt, so wiring, sensing and the power stage are all suspects. The pump stops and auto-stop is blocked. P0B07/P0B08 are the low and high variants, P0B00 and P0B03 phases U and V.

causes.label: Poor contact in the phase W lead or pump connector
Current sensing in the pump inverter faulty
Phase W power stage in the pump control module faulty
Winding fault in phase W of the pump motor

symptoms: MIL or transmission/hybrid warning
Engine keeps running at stops, no auto-stop

P0B07.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase W Current Low
P0B07.description: P0B07 means phase W of the auxiliary fluid pump motor carries less current than commanded, the typical sign of an open W path. GM uses it on the Volt and later hybrids: below 1 A peak W-axis current for 0.4 s of 0.6 s, with the inverter in normal PWM above 50 V, sets a Type A fault. A GM service update for the 2017-18 Cadillac CT6 plug-in shows the code had been calibrated off; a W phase loss then shut the car down or prevented starting with no code and no MIL, until reprogramming of the drive motor power inverter module enabled P0B07 as Type A. On the 2014-15 Spark EV, bulletin PI1433 ties P0B01, P0B04 or P0B07 to an unlatched pump connector. P0B01 and P0B04 are phases U and V, P0B08 the high side, P0B06 the general W code.

causes.label: Pump motor connector not fully seated or latched (Chevrolet Spark EV)
Open circuit in the phase W lead or terminal
Outdated inverter software (Cadillac CT6 plug-in, service update 18199)
Open winding of phase W in the pump motor

symptoms: MIL and Service Vehicle Soon light
Loss of propulsion, vehicle shutdown or no-start

P0B08.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Phase W Current High
P0B08.description: P0B08 is set when the current in phase W of the auxiliary transmission fluid pump motor rises above the permitted limit. No manufacturer documents this exact code in public sources. In GM's 2016 Volt calibration the equivalent protection is P0C28, which fails on any phase above 35 A or on a d-axis current below a temperature-dependent limit, both within milliseconds to protect the IGBTs. A W-specific high code points to a short in the W lead or winding, a binding pump or a sensing error; the Hitachi patent shows the W value may be calculated rather than measured directly. CARB requires such output drivers to be monitored for circuit faults. The pump shuts down, so start-stop and electric driving are restricted. P0B07 is the low side, P0B02 and P0B05 phases U and V.

causes.label: Phase W lead shorted to another phase or to ground
Pump binding mechanically, raising motor current
Current sensing in the pump inverter reads too high
Shorted turns in phase W of the pump motor

symptoms: MIL and transmission or hybrid warning
Auxiliary pump shuts down, auto-stop disabled

P0B09.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P0B09.description: P0B09 concerns the power feed of auxiliary pump A's motor: the controller sees no valid supply voltage, usually because the circuit is open. GM documents it for its 2012-13 eAssist mild hybrids (BAS Plus): the hardware input reports an out-of-range voltage flag on the auxiliary pump circuit, enabled with ignition voltage above 9 V; failing for at least 0.375 s within a 1.2 s sample sets P0B09 as Type B, MIL after two trips. A related GM check, P2797, verifies during auto-stops that the pump draws power and that turbine speed does not flare on restart. A Hitachi patent on a battery-fed sub-oil pump shows the controller inhibits engine auto-stop when pump current behaves abnormally. Typical results: no auto-stop and a lamp. P0B0A/P0B0B are the low and high variants.

causes.label: Blown fuse or open relay in the pump supply
Open supply wire or loose terminal at the pump connector
Poor ground connection of the pump motor
Voltage sensing input in the controller faulty

symptoms: Engine auto-stop no longer occurs
MIL after two drive cycles
Shift flare or delayed drive engagement on restart

P0B0A.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P0B0A.description: P0B0A means the supply voltage measured at the motor of auxiliary pump A is lower than expected while the pump should be running. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's eAssist tables only cover the open-circuit case as P0B09. A Mikuni patent shows why the controller measures this voltage at all: it combines motor current, supply voltage and speed to judge the hydraulic load, so a sagging supply also falsifies pump diagnosis. Causes are high resistance in the feed or ground, a weak 12 V battery, a failing DC/DC converter or a voltage drop when the pump starts. CARB requires circuit checks on such outputs. The pump runs slowly or not at all and start-stop is usually inhibited. P0B09 covers an open circuit, P0B0B a supply that is too high, P0562 low system voltage in general.

causes.label: Corroded terminal or high resistance in the pump feed or ground
Weak 12 V battery or poor charging
DC/DC converter or alternator output too low (hybrid)
Voltage sensing input in the controller faulty

symptoms: Start-stop function inactive
MIL or transmission warning
Jerky drive-off after an engine stop

P0B0B.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Motor Supply Voltage Circuit High
P0B0B.description: P0B0B reports a supply voltage at the motor of auxiliary pump A that is above the expected range. Subaru documents it on the 2014-15 XV Crosstrek Hybrid (bulletin 16-94-15R), together with P172A: a leaking O-ring at the electric oil pump relief valve can let CVT fluid into the pump motor. The check removes the three U, V and W cables at the oil pump inverter and reads AC voltage across them with the engine held at 1800 rpm in Park; 0.5 V or more means the drive motor and case assembly with the damaged seal must be replaced, less means the cause lies elsewhere. Subaru adds that P0C79, drive motor inverter voltage too high, appears only together with these codes and does not mean the inverter is faulty. P0B09 and P0B0A are the open and low variants.

causes.label: CVT fluid entering the pump motor via a leaking relief valve O-ring (Subaru XV Crosstrek Hybrid)
Supply circuit shorted to a higher voltage source
Oil pump inverter or its voltage sensing faulty

symptoms: Warning lamp on, hybrid or CVT function restricted
Possibly P0C79 stored at the same time

P0B0C.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump A Hydraulic Leakage
P0B0C.description: P0B0C says the circuit fed by auxiliary pump A loses pressure through a leak, so the pump cannot hold the demanded pressure. Stellantis documents it as P0B0C 7A for the 2023-26 Jeep Avenger and 2026 Compass with hybrid dual-clutch transmission outside the US (TSB 21-061-26): an internal leak at the parking pawl locking piston causes jerking and power loss and may stop the engine from restarting after a stop; with P07E4 or P07E6 present and more than 5 km on the clock, the piston or the transmission is replaced. How a controller can see a leak shows a Nidec patent: after a speed change the pump current keeps falling instead of recovering, and the pump is stopped. P0B0B and P0B09 cover the supply, P2797 a pump that does not deliver.

causes.label: Internal leak at the parking pawl locking piston (Jeep Avenger/Compass hybrid DCT)
Worn seal or valve leaking inside the hydraulic circuit
External leak and low transmission fluid level
Internal wear of the auxiliary pump

symptoms: Jerking and loss of power while driving
Engine fails to restart after a stop
Transmission warning, possibly with P07E4 or P07E6

P0B0D.title: Electric/Auxiliary Transmission Fluid Pump Motor Control Module
P0B0D.description: P0B0D is an internal fault of the module that drives the auxiliary pump motor. GM documents it for the auxiliary transmission pump controller (ATPC) in its 2011 and 2014 hybrid tables and for the 2016 Cadillac ELR: it checks processor integrity, such as SPI hardware faults or a wrong seed and key between processors, with more than 9.5 V supply; 28 failures out of 32 samples in a 6.25 ms loop, detected within about 200 ms, set a Type A fault. Stellantis lists P0B0D-00 on the 2021-25 Jeep Wrangler 4xe and 2022-25 Grand Cherokee 4xe with the 8P75PH plug-in transmission (TSB 21-038-25, revised 21-041-26): MIL and limp mode, sometimes with U0287; the fix is a new in-pan electric pump. U0287 is lost communication with the pump module, P0C23 to P0C25 its circuit.

causes.label: Electric pump with integrated control electronics failed (Jeep 4xe 8P75PH)
Processor or memory fault inside the pump control module
Supply voltage dips or poor ground at the module

symptoms: MIL on
Transmission in limp mode
Possibly lost communication with the pump module (U0287)

P0B0E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit
P0B0E.description: Many packs measure current with two channels or two sensors so the controller can cross-check them; sensor B is the second channel next to sensor A (P0ABF to P0AC3). P0B0E is its general circuit code. Toyota uses it as the base of internal codes on the 2020-25 RAV4 Hybrid: the sensor sends a voltage rising with current on channel IB0 (sensor A) and an inverse one on IB1 (sensor B). P0B0E11 (IB1 too low) and P0B0E15 (IB1 too high or open) are reported to a generic scan tool as P0B10 and P0B11, one trip, MIL on. GM monitors its fine-range channel B with P0B10, P0B11 and the A/B correlation P0B13. CARB requires circuit monitoring. State of charge then becomes uncertain.

causes.label: Signal or ground wire of channel B damaged or connector loose
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective
Sensor supply voltage faulty
Battery ECU input defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery power limited, less electric assist
Implausible state-of-charge display

P0B0F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P0B0F.description: P0B0F flags a current sensor B signal that is electrically in range but implausible, for example an offset at zero current or a value that does not match the other measurement. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM handles comparable faults differently: on its dual-range sensor, the 2019 table P0B13 compares sensors A and B and fails when they differ by more than 10 A while both read between -20 and 20 A, 400 of 500 samples at 25 ms, Type A; offset errors of sensor A are P0AC0. CARB requires rationality checks for hybrid battery inputs. A drifting current reading corrupts the state-of-charge calculation, so the controller tends to narrow the usable battery window.

causes.label: Current sensor B offset drift or ageing
Ground offset or high resistance in the sensor wiring
Sensor displaced on the busbar or magnetic interference

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning, MIL possible
State of charge jumps or drifts
Reduced battery power

P0B10.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit Low
P0B10.description: P0B10 means the output of current sensor B lies below its valid range. GM uses a dual-range Hall sensor whose channel B covers small currents with high resolution: the 2019 battery energy control module table sets P0B10 when this fine current reads below -24 A (ADC count under 82) for 1.6 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; the 2011 Volt table uses -23 A for 175 ms within 250 ms, one trip. Toyota reports P0B10 for the 2020-25 RAV4 Hybrid when the inverse channel IB1 voltage is excessively low (internal code P0B0E11), one trip, MIL on immediately. A short to ground or a lost sensor supply is typical. The high-side code is P0B11.

causes.label: Sensor B signal line shorted to ground
5 V supply of the current sensor missing
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery charge and discharge power limited
Engine runs more often, fuel use rises

P0B11.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit High
P0B11.description: P0B11 is set when current sensor B delivers a signal above its valid range. In GM's dual-range design, channel B is the fine channel for small currents: the 2019 battery energy control module table fails it above +24 A (ADC count over 4013) for 1.6 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, and the 2011 Volt table above +23 A for 175 ms within 250 ms, one trip. Toyota maps its internal code P0B0E15, excessively high or open IB1 channel voltage, to P0B11 on the 2020-25 RAV4 Hybrid, with one-trip logic and immediate MIL. An open ground, a signal shorted to the supply or a failed sensor are typical. The low-side code is P0B10, the sensor A equivalent P0AC2.

causes.label: Open signal or ground wire of sensor B
Signal line shorted to the sensor supply or 12 V
Current sensor or junction block with integrated sensor defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning on
Battery power limited, less electric driving
Implausible state-of-charge display

P0B12.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B12.description: P0B12 covers a current sensor B signal that jumps or drops out in a way real current cannot, typically from a loose connector, a chafed signal wire or noise on the sensor ground. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM monitors its sensor B channel with the range limits P0B10 and P0B11 and compares it with sensor A through P0B13, which fails above a 10 A difference in 400 of 500 samples, Type A; an erratic channel often shows up there first. CARB requires circuit and rationality monitoring for hybrid battery inputs. Because the fault comes and goes, the code may be the only trace, but during dropouts the controller can still cut battery power or light a warning.

causes.label: Loose connector or poor terminal contact at the current sensor
Chafed signal or ground wire
Electrical noise on the sensor ground

symptoms: Intermittent hybrid or EV warning
Short power reductions during dropouts
Code stored without lasting symptoms

P0B13.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Current Sensor A/B Correlation
P0B13.description: P0B13 compares the two pack current readings, sensor A and sensor B, and sets when they disagree. On the Chevrolet Volt GM pairs a coarse and a fine channel: the code fails when they differ by more than 10 A while both read between -20 and 20 A, for example 10 s within a 12.5 s window (2016) or 400 of 500 samples at 25 ms (2019), Type A, one trip. Bulletins show P0B13 on the GM Lyriq, Hummer EV and BrightDrop Zevo after suspect public chargers, and on the Audi Q5 PHEV and e-tron GT, where software of the battery controller caused it. Single-sensor faults use P0ABF to P0AC3 and P0B0E to P0B12. The driver sees a high-voltage warning and reduced power.

causes.label: Battery controller software fault, fixed by update (Audi, GM)
Disturbance from an external charging station during charging
Offset drift of one of the two current channels
Internal communication fault between switching unit and current sensor

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Red battery or Service High Voltage message, request to stop safely
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Charging interrupted or refused

P0B14.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit
P0B14.description: SAE J2012 reserves up to four pack voltage measurements, A to D; voltage sense B is the second one. P0B14 is its general circuit code: the battery controller sees an electrical fault on this input, typically an open or implausible raw signal. Which tap a manufacturer calls B is not standardised. No manufacturer documents P0B14 publicly. For the comparable channel A GM checks pack-side voltage against fixed limits and against the sum of cell voltages (P0ABB to P0ABD). CARB requires battery voltage sensors of hybrid storage systems to be monitored like any input component. Range, low, high and erratic faults have their own codes, P0B15 to P0B18. The system usually limits or blocks high-voltage operation.

causes.label: Voltage sense lead or its fuse open inside the pack
Sense connector at the battery controller loose or corroded
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B15.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit Range/Performance
P0B15.description: P0B15 marks pack voltage measurement B as electrically valid but implausible: the value lies within the sensor range yet does not match a reference, typically the sum of the cell voltages or another pack measurement. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM shows the principle on channel A: P0ABB fails when pack voltage and summed cell voltages differ by more than 12 V, 20 of 25 samples at 25 ms, Type A, one trip. CARB demands rationality checks for battery voltage sensors of the hybrid storage system. Hard circuit faults of channel B are P0B14, P0B16 and P0B17. Because state of charge and cell protection rely on this value, the controller restricts power or charging.

causes.label: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel B
Faulty cell voltage acquisition distorts the reference sum
Increased contact resistance at sense terminals
Battery controller software needs an update

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Implausible state-of-charge or range display

P0B16.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit Low
P0B16.description: P0B16 sets when pack voltage measurement B reports a value below its plausible minimum, usually an electrical cause such as a sense lead shorted to ground or an open input that pulls the reading down. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM uses the same logic on channel A: on its BECM P0ABC sets when the pack-side voltage drops below 24 V for 1.6 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip. CARB requires out-of-range monitoring of battery voltage sensors in hybrid storage systems. The opposite fault is P0B17, implausible but in-range values are P0B15. Without a trustworthy pack voltage the controller may refuse to close the contactors or limit operation.

causes.label: Sense lead of channel B shorted to ground
Fuse or resistor in the sense path open
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B17.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit High
P0B17.description: P0B17 means pack voltage measurement B reads above its plausible maximum. Mercedes-Benz uses this exact code on the eSprinter 907: inaccurate BMS measurements can store P0B171C, voltage sensor B in the high-voltage battery module shorted to positive with the value out of range, together with P0ABD00 for sensor A. The result is an intermittent no-start or no Ready status, fixed by a BMS software update. GM checks channel A against 479 V on its BECM (P0ABD, Type A). CARB requires out-of-range monitoring of battery voltage sensors. The low counterpart is P0B16. A real overvoltage is not implied; the measurement itself is suspect.

causes.label: BMS measurement inaccuracy, fixed by software update (Mercedes eSprinter)
Sense lead of channel B shorted to a higher potential
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system
MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B18.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B18.description: P0B18 reports that pack voltage measurement B jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing steadily. The controller detects implausibly fast changes or short signal losses that disappear again, so the fault often shows up as a history code. No manufacturer documents P0B18 publicly; GM, for example, monitors only channel A in its published tables (P0ABB to P0ABD). CARB requires battery voltage sensors of the hybrid storage system to be monitored for circuit faults. Steady faults of channel B use P0B14 to P0B17. Typical triggers are loose sense connectors or chafed leads that react to vibration and temperature, so symptoms come and go.

causes.label: Loose or corroded sense connector
Sense lead chafed, intermittent contact
Battery controller software misinterprets transients

symptoms: Warning appears and disappears, often stored as history
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B19.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit
P0B19.description: Voltage sense C is the third of up to four pack voltage measurements defined in SAE J2012. P0B19 is its general circuit code and sets when the battery controller finds this input electrically unusable, for instance open or without a valid raw value. Which measuring point a manufacturer assigns to C is its own choice. No manufacturer documents P0B19 publicly. GM shows the principle for channel A, checking pack-side voltage against limits and against the summed cell voltages (P0ABB to P0ABD). CARB requires battery voltage sensors of hybrid storage systems to be monitored as input components. The detailed fault types of channel C are P0B1A to P0B1D. High-voltage operation is usually limited.

causes.label: Voltage sense lead C or its fuse open
Sense connector loose or corroded
Measurement input of the battery controller defective

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist
Vehicle may not reach Ready or may shut down the high-voltage system

P0B1A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit Range/Performance
P0B1A.description: P0B1A flags pack voltage measurement C as in range but not believable. The controller compares it with a reference, usually the sum of the cell voltages or another pack voltage reading, and sets the code when the difference stays too large. No manufacturer documents P0B1A publicly. As an analogue, GM fails P0ABB on channel A once pack voltage and summed cell voltages differ by more than 12 V for 20 of 25 samples, Type A. CARB requires rationality monitoring for battery voltage sensors of hybrid storage systems. Electrical faults of channel C are P0B19, P0B1B and P0B1C. A distorted pack voltage undermines state of charge and cell protection, so power or charging is restricted.

causes.label: Drift or calibration error of measurement channel C
Cell voltage acquisition faulty, reference sum wrong
Increased resistance at sense terminals
Battery controller software needs an update

symptoms: MIL and hybrid/EV system warning on
Implausible state-of-charge or range display
Battery power limited, reduced electric drive or assist

P0B1B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit Low
P0B1B.description: P0B1B sets when pack voltage measurement C delivers a reading below its plausible lower limit. Typical electrical causes are a sense lead shorted to ground, an open fuse or resistor in the sense path, or a defective controller input. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM applies the same idea to channel A, where P0ABC sets below 24 V pack-side voltage for 1.6 s in a 2 s window, Type A. CARB calls for out-of-range monitoring of battery voltage sensors. P0B1C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit High
P0B1C.description: P0B1C reports that pack voltage measurement C reads above its plausible upper limit. P0B1D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B1D.description: P0B1D stands for an unsteady pack voltage measurement C: the signal jumps, drops out for moments or changes faster than a real battery voltage can. P0B1E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit
P0B1E.description: Voltage sense D is the fourth and last pack voltage measurement in the SAE J2012 scheme. P0B1E is its general circuit code: the battery controller treats this input as electrically faulty, for example open or without a usable raw signal. The assignment of D to a specific measuring point is manufacturer-specific. No manufacturer documents P0B1E publicly. GM illustrates the monitoring on channel A, comparing pack-side voltage with limits and with the summed cell voltages (P0ABB to P0ABD). P0B1F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Sense D Circuit Range/Performance

Bentley documents it in the 48 V Dynamic Ride system of the Continental GT and Flying Spur, stored in address 0021 with symptom code 28672; the prescribed repair is replacing the super capacitor. It covers a voltage that does not match expectation without saying whether it is unstable (P0B28), too low (P0B29) or too high (P0B2A). P0B28.title: Hybrid/EV Battery B Voltage Unstable

Stellantis documents it with P0B28-00 on the Jeep Wrangler 4xe: the MIL is on, and the bulletin warns that after 49 days with this MIL lit the vehicle is no longer allowed to start. P0B29.title: Hybrid/EV Battery B Voltage Low

It is the low counterpart to P0B2A; fluctuating readings belong to P0B28 and the general fault to P0B27. It mirrors P0B29 (too low), while P0B28 covers fluctuation and P0B27 the general fault. P0B2B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery C Voltage

It signals an implausible voltage of this unit without the detail given by P0B2C (unstable), P0B2D (low) or P0B2E (high). P0B2C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery C Voltage Unstable
P0B2C.description: P0B2C indicates that the voltage of hybrid/EV battery C is unstable, meaning it changes faster or further than plausible for the current load, while a steady deviation would set P0B2D or P0B2E. No manufacturer documents P0B2C publicly. P0B2D.description: P0B2D means the voltage of hybrid/EV battery C is too low compared with what the controller expects. High readings of the same unit are P0B2E, fluctuating ones P0B2C. P0B33.title: High Voltage Service Disconnect Circuit
P0B33.description: The high-voltage service disconnect is the removable plug, usually fused, that splits the traction battery for safe servicing. P0B34.title: High Voltage Service Disconnect Circuit Performance

P0B37.title: High Voltage Service Disconnect Open

Service disconnect plug removed, loose or not locked
Open terminal in the plug base or interlock connector
Battery energy control module fault

symptoms: Intermittent stall or no crank
Stop Safely Now message and MIL
High-voltage interlock code stored in another module

P0B38.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
P0B38.description: Hybrid and electric drives cool the inverter and motor electronics with electric coolant pumps; J2012 numbers them A, B and C. P0B38 sets when the controller detects an open or general fault in the control line of pump B, typically by checking the driver output for missing load current. No manufacturer documents P0B38 publicly. FCA uses a pump B on the Jeep Compass and Renegade 4xe, where bulletins name its performance code P0C74, and Mercedes uses the pump A code P0A05 for an open control circuit of the low-temperature circuit pump on M264 engines. CARB requires output components of inverter thermal management to be monitored. Expect a coolant or hybrid warning and power reduction if electronics overheat.

causes.label: Pump connector loose, corroded or terminal pushed out
Open control wire between controller and pump
Pump electronics or motor failed open
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty

symptoms: Hybrid system or coolant warning, MIL on
Reduced electric drive power when electronics get hot
Pump not running audibly after switch-on

P0B39.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P0B39.description: P0B39 sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B is lower than the controller expects, usually a short to ground on the command line or a pump input that pulls the line down. On a low-side switched or PWM line the module sees the voltage stuck low while it commands the pump off. No manufacturer documents P0B39 publicly. Pump B is in service at FCA (Compass and Renegade 4xe, performance code P0C74), and Ford stores the pump A codes P0A06 and P0A07 in the PCM of the 2020 Explorer and Aviator hybrids. CARB requires these inverter cooling outputs to be checked for circuit faults. Open and high faults are P0B38 and P0B3A; running faults use P0C74 and P2D05 ff.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to ground, often chafed at brackets
Pump electronics pulling the control input low
Coolant or water in the pump connector
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or coolant warning
Pump runs permanently or not at all, depending on circuit design
Power limitation at high load or heat

P0B3A.title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High
P0B3A.description: P0B3A sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B stays higher than expected, typically a short to battery voltage on the command line or, with some driver designs, an open pump input that floats high. The module then cannot switch the pump as requested. No manufacturer documents P0B3A publicly. As reference points, FCA has a pump B on its 4xe models with the performance code P0C74, and Ford lists the pump A high code P0A07 among PCM codes fixed by a battery controller update on the 2020 Explorer and Aviator hybrids. CARB requires inverter thermal management outputs to be monitored. Open and low faults are P0B38 and P0B39. Overheating protection may reduce power.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Pump control input open so the line floats high
Controller software misjudging the circuit, fixed by update
Driver stage in the controlling module faulty

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or coolant warning
Pump cannot be switched off or on as commanded
Reduced electric power when the inverter heats up

P0B3B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit
P0B3B.description: Voltage sense A to Z and beyond are the cell or cell-group sense channels of the battery monitoring electronics, unlike the pack voltage sense codes P0ABA and P0B14 ff, which measure the whole pack. P0B3B is the circuit code for channel A. GM uses it in the battery energy control module as an open sense line check: neighbouring cell readings differ by 1.3 V or more, or a cell reads under 36 mV with balancing on, or a splice reads over 0.1 V (bus bar 0.5 V), for 0.6 s; Type A, one trip. Ford stores P0B3B with other open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV and 2023 Mach-E; Honda's 2014-2015 Accord Hybrid used it for a cell voltage sensor fault caused by inverter noise.

causes.label: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack
Intermittent fault in the flexible printed circuit to the battery controller (Ford Mach-E)
Sensor software misreading inverter noise, fixed by update (Honda)
Internal failure of the traction battery requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: MIL or powertrain warning, Stop Safely Now message possible
No start or no charging
Fail-safe EV mode with limited speed and sudden loss of power

P0B3C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Range/Performance
P0B3C.description: P0B3C flags a cell voltage channel A that reads plausible values but does not follow the other cells. GM runs this check in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 as a stuck-in-range test: while the average cell voltage moves by at least 0.005 V in one direction between samples, channel A must move as well; 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip. FCA names the code Voltage Sense 1 Circuit Performance on the Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid and fixes it, together with P0B41 and further channels, by reprogramming the battery pack control module. Circuit, low, high and erratic faults have their own codes. The system limits battery power or shuts down hybrid operation.

causes.label: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica)
Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics
High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection
Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack

symptoms: MIL on, often with several voltage sense codes
Reduced electric range or no electric drive
Contactor related codes stored at the same time

P0B3D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Low
P0B3D.description: P0B3D sets when cell voltage channel A reads below the lowest value a real cell can have, which points to the measurement rather than the cell. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, provided no open sense line, communication or balancing fault is active. FCA lists P0B3D as Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Low on the 2019 Ram 1500 with eTorque mild hybrid, next to the pack-level code P0ABA, and cures it with a battery pack control module update. A genuinely low cell is reported with separate cell voltage codes. Expect reduced or blocked hybrid assist.

causes.label: Battery pack control module software, fixed by update (Ram eTorque)
Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

symptoms: MIL on
Start-stop and electric assist unavailable
Hybrid battery power limited

P0B3E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit High
P0B3E.description: P0B3E sets when cell voltage channel A reads above any value a healthy lithium-ion cell reaches, so the reading is treated as a sensing fault. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip. FCA uses the code on the 2021 Jeep Wrangler 4xe as Voltage Sense 1 Circuit High and on the 2019 Ram 1500 eTorque as Voltage Sense A Circuit High; in both cases a battery pack control module update removes a false MIL. A truly overcharged cell sets separate cell voltage high codes such as P0DE7 instead. Low, range and open faults are P0B3D, P0B3C and P0B3B. The car limits battery use.

causes.label: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA)
Open sense line letting the input float high
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

symptoms: MIL on, possibly without noticeable drivability change
Electric drive or start-stop disabled
Charging limited

P0B3F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B3F.description: P0B3F is reserved for a cell voltage channel A that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing steadily. No manufacturer documents P0B3F publicly. GM's 2019 tables show how the siblings on the same channel work: an open line test (P0B3B), a stuck-in-range test against the other cells (P0B3C) and fixed limits of 0.2 V and 4.8 V (P0B3D, P0B3E); an erratic test would watch for implausible jumps between samples. CARB requires battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system to be monitored as input components, with fault codes pinpointing the smallest replaceable unit. Loose connections at the cell taps or the monitoring board are the usual suspects. Hybrid power may be limited.

causes.label: Loose or cracked cell tap connection
Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector
Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines

symptoms: MIL or hybrid warning that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive or assist

P0B40.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit
P0B40.description: P0B40 is the circuit code of cell voltage sense channel B, the second cell or cell group the battery monitoring electronics measures; pack-level voltage uses P0ABA and P0B14 ff instead. GM applies the same open sense line test as on channel A: a 1.3 V jump between neighbouring cells, under 36 mV with balancing on, or splice voltage above 0.1 V (bus bar 0.5 V) for 0.6 s, Type A, one trip. Ford lists P0B40 among the open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV, where the fix is a new traction battery, and on the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and e-Transit, where an intermittent flexible printed circuit cable in the battery controller is to blame. Expect no start or no charging.

causes.label: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack
Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable in the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, e-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure requiring replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: Wrench indicator or MIL, Stop Safely Now message possible
No start condition
Battery cannot be charged

P0B41.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Range/Performance
P0B41.description: P0B41 reports that cell voltage channel B gives values inside the normal range that fail a plausibility check against the other cells. In GM's 2019 tables Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 compares sample-to-sample changes: if the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V while channel B stays unchanged, a failure is counted, and 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip, with system voltage above 10.2 V. FCA calls it Voltage Sense 2 Circuit Performance on the Pacifica plug-in hybrid and lists it with P0B3C and further channels in battery pack control module update bulletins. Circuit, low, high and erratic faults of channel B are P0B40, P0B42, P0B43 and P0B44.

causes.label: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica)
Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics
High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection
Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack

symptoms: MIL on, often with several voltage sense codes
Electric drive reduced or unavailable
Contactor related codes stored at the same time

P0B42.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Low
P0B42.description: P0B42 sets when cell voltage channel B reads implausibly low, below what any usable cell would show. GM's battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, and only when no open sense line, slave communication or balancing fault is present. FCA uses P0B42 as Voltage Sense 2 Circuit Low on the 2022 Grand Wagoneer and Wagoneer with the 5.7 L eTorque mild hybrid; its bulletin calls the MIL false, mentions inoperative start-stop and a car that seems to run on fuel only, and prescribes a battery pack control module update. Cells that are actually weak set separate cell voltage codes. High and range faults are P0B43 and P0B41.

causes.label: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA eTorque)
Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

symptoms: MIL on
Start-stop inoperative
Vehicle behaves as if running on the engine only

P0B43.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit High
P0B43.description: P0B43 sets when cell voltage channel B reads higher than a lithium-ion cell can physically reach in service, so the controller blames the measurement path. GM documents the criteria for its battery energy control module: cell voltage B at 4.8 V or above for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, with open sense line, communication and balancing faults ruled out first. Beyond GM, no manufacturer documents P0B43 publicly; FCA's sister code P0B3E for channel A shows that software in the battery controller can cause such readings. CARB treats battery voltage sensors as monitored input components. Overcharged cells use separate cell voltage codes. Low, range and open faults of channel B are P0B42, P0B41 and P0B40.

causes.label: Open sense line letting the input float high
Battery controller software misreading the channel
Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed

symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning on
Charging or electric drive limited

P0B44.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B44.description: P0B44 is the J2012 slot for a cell voltage channel B whose reading jumps or drops out for short moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents P0B44 publicly. For orientation, GM's 2019 tables check channel B for open sense lines (P0B40), frozen values compared with the other cells (P0B41) and fixed limits of 0.2 V and 4.8 V (P0B42, P0B43); an erratic monitor would add a test for implausible steps between samples. CARB requires the storage system's voltage sensors to be monitored as inputs and faults to be pinpointed to the smallest replaceable unit. Typical causes are vibration-loosened cell taps and connectors on the monitoring board. Warnings may come and go with driving conditions.

causes.label: Loose or cracked cell tap connection
Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector
Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines

symptoms: MIL or hybrid warning that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive or assist

P0B45.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit
P0B45.description: Voltage sense C is the third cell or cell-group measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics, not a pack voltage input like P0ABA. P0B45 reports an electrical break in that channel. GM's battery energy control module sets it when its open sense line test fails for 0.6 s: adjacent cell readings at least 1.3 V apart, a cell below 36 mV while its balancing switch is on, or a splice above 0.1 V (bus bar splice 0.5 V); Type A, one trip. Ford lists P0B45 with the other open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid, fixed by a new traction battery, and on the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit, where an intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit is blamed. Expect no start or no charging.

causes.label: Open cell sense tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel C
Intermittent flexible printed circuit between cells and battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: Vehicle does not start or does not become ready to drive
High-voltage battery no longer charges
Powertrain warning (wrench) and Stop Safely Now message

P0B46.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Range/Performance
P0B46.description: With P0B46 the channel C wiring is intact; the value on it looks plausible but no longer behaves like a real cell. GM's 2019 tables run the test in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2: whenever the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V in one direction, channel C has to follow; if it stays frozen in 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms, the code sets, Type A. The 2016 Chevrolet Volt uses a window of 7 out of 8 seconds instead. Chrysler calls the code Voltage Sense 3 Circuit Performance on the 2020 Pacifica plug-in hybrid and cures it by reflashing the battery pack control module. So before opening the battery, check the controller software level.

causes.label: Battery controller software misjudging the channel, fixed by reflash (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Measuring chip input for channel C stuck at a constant value
High-resistance cell tap damping the channel C signal

symptoms: MIL on without noticeable driving fault
Reduced electric power or hybrid assist
Contactor or precharge codes stored at the same time (Pacifica)

P0B47.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Low
P0B47.description: P0B47 is stored when channel C delivers a voltage too low to come from a working cell or block, so the controller blames the measurement rather than the battery. GM documents two implementations. On lithium-ion packs the battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, one trip, unless an open sense line, communication or balancing fault is already active. On the 2012 Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra two-mode hybrids channel C is nickel-metal hydride block 3; there block 3 and block 4 must both read under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips. Shorted sense lines or a failed measuring input are the usual suspects.

causes.label: Sense lines of channel C shorted to each other or to a neighbouring tap
Failed measuring input in the battery monitoring module
Loose or corroded block connector shared by blocks 3 and 4 (GM two-mode)

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Electric drive or engine start-stop no longer available
Battery power limited, sluggish acceleration

P0B48.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit High
P0B48.description: No healthy lithium-ion cell reaches 4.8 V, which is why GM's battery energy control module treats a channel C reading of 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window as a sensing fault and stores P0B48, Type A, one trip. On the 2012 two-mode full-size hybrids the threshold is scaled to a nickel-metal hydride block: block 3 above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips. Because the controller cannot trust the reading, it usually narrows the allowed charge and discharge power to protect the cells. For the driver this means less electric assist and possibly no plug-in charging. A cell that is really overcharged triggers separate cell voltage codes, not this one.

causes.label: Channel C sense line touching a tap of higher potential
Failed measuring input or reference in the monitoring electronics
Monitoring software fault, check for controller updates

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced charge and discharge power
Plug-in charging refused

P0B49.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B49.description: P0B49 is reserved for a channel C signal that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing for good. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, which uses the other four channel C codes, has no erratic test for it in its published tables. A technician would start from the freeze frame and log cell voltage C next to its neighbours while flexing the module harness, because a loose crimp or a cracked solder joint on the monitoring board shows up as spikes that a permanent test misses. CARB requires battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system to be monitored like any input and faults to be tied to the smallest replaceable unit. Warnings may come and go.

causes.label: Loose crimp or connector on the channel C sense line
Cracked solder joint on the cell monitoring board
Electrical noise from the inverter coupling into the sense line

symptoms: Warning light that appears and disappears
Occasional short loss of electric drive power

P0B4A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit
P0B4A.description: P0B4A is the open-circuit code of cell sense channel D, the fourth measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics. GM checks it in the battery energy control module with the same open sense line logic as the other channels: a gap of 1.3 V or more between adjacent cells, under 36 mV on a cell being balanced, or splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V at a bus bar, for 0.6 s, Type A. For diagnosis, the pattern matters: if P0B4A stands alone, inspect the channel D tap and its connector; if Ford's whole open-line group from P0B3B upwards is set, as on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV or the 2023 Mach-E and E-Transit, a common cause such as the BECM flex cable or the battery itself is more likely.

causes.label: Open channel D sense tap or connector (code set alone)
Faulty BECM flexible printed circuit affecting several channels (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery fault (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: No start or vehicle will not go into ready mode
Charging not possible
Several sense channel codes stored together

P0B4B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Range/Performance
P0B4B.description: How the plausibility of channel D is judged depends on the pack. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids the battery pack control module multiplies block 4 by 20 and compares it with the pack voltage; a gap above 70 V in 160 of 170 samples sets P0B4B, Type B, two trips. Later lithium-ion packs compare movement instead: in the 2016 Cadillac ELR channel D must move with the average cell voltage, checked every 200 ms with 20 failures in 40 samples, Type A, and the 2019 tables use 35 of 40 samples. Chrysler lists the code as Voltage Sense 4 Circuit Performance on the 2020 Pacifica plug-in hybrid and fixes it with BPCM software. Separate codes cover open, low and high faults.

causes.label: Outdated battery controller software (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Block or cell voltage measurement drifting away from the pack voltage
Measuring input of channel D frozen at a constant value

symptoms: MIL, often after several drives
Limited hybrid assist or electric range

P0B4C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Low
P0B4C.description: From the driver's seat P0B4C looks like a battery problem: the hybrid warning comes on and electric power is cut back. Technically it is a measuring fault on cell channel D, whose reading has fallen below what even a deeply discharged cell would show. GM's battery energy control module uses 0.2 V or less, held for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, and skips the test while open sense line or communication faults are active. On the 2012 two-mode full-size hybrids, channel D is block 4, and the code needs blocks 4 and 5 both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. A genuinely weak cell produces separate cell voltage codes, so P0B4C points to wiring or the monitoring module.

causes.label: Short between channel D sense line and a neighbouring line
Defective input on the cell monitoring module
Corroded tap shared by blocks 4 and 5 (GM two-mode)

symptoms: Hybrid warning message and MIL
Electric power and regeneration cut back
Engine runs more often than usual

P0B4D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit High
P0B4D.description: P0B4D sets when cell sense channel D reports more voltage than the cell or block behind it can deliver. GM's limits are 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s on lithium-ion packs (battery energy control module, Type A, one trip) and above 23 V for block 4 of the 2012 two-mode hybrids (15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips). A practical first check is live data: if channel D sits far above its neighbours while the pack voltage and the other channels look normal, the fault is in the sense path, not in the cells. Typical findings are a sense lead that contacts a higher tap or a damaged measuring input. The controller limits power until the code is repaired.

causes.label: Channel D sense lead contacting a tap of higher potential
Damaged measuring input in the monitoring electronics
Moisture or contamination on the monitoring board creating leakage paths

symptoms: MIL and battery system warning
Reduced acceleration and regenerative braking
Charging power limited or charging refused

P0B4E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B4E.description: P0B4E completes the five-code set of cell channel D. Where P0B4A means a lasting open circuit, P0B4B a frozen or implausible value and P0B4C or P0B4D a reading beyond fixed limits, this code is meant for short, irregular dropouts and spikes. No manufacturer documents P0B4E publicly, and GM's published hybrid tables, which cover the other four, contain no such test. CARB obliges manufacturers to monitor the storage system's voltage sensors as input components. In practice, intermittent sense faults trace back to vibration, thermal cycling and connectors that only lose contact on rough roads, which is why the fault often cannot be reproduced in the workshop.

causes.label: Connector or tap losing contact under vibration
Solder joint or crimp cracked by thermal cycling

symptoms: Intermittent hybrid warning, often on rough roads
Fault not reproducible during workshop test

P0B4F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit
P0B4F.description: Cell sense channel E is the fifth measuring path between the battery cells and the monitoring electronics; P0B4F means the controller sees it as electrically open. Ford's experience shows how serious this can be: on 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids P0B4F appears among up to fourteen open-line codes from P0B3B to P0B7C with a no-start condition, and the bulletin prescribes replacing the high-voltage battery. On the 2023 Mach-E and E-Transit the same family points to an intermittent flexible circuit at the BECM. GM's BECM logic needs 0.6 s of an open-line pattern, such as adjacent cells 1.3 V apart or a balanced cell under 36 mV, and stores the code as Type A.

causes.label: Internal failure of the high-voltage battery (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Broken channel E sense lead, splice or bus bar contact

symptoms: No start
Battery cannot be charged
Stop Safely Now message while driving

P0B50.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit Range/Performance
P0B50.description: On the 2020 Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid P0B50 is called Voltage Sense 5 Circuit Performance and rarely comes alone: the FCA bulletin lists it with the other sense channels, contactor stuck codes, a long precharge time and wake-up circuit faults, all cured by updating the battery pack control module. Some owners also notice that scheduled charging fails because the pack does not wake up. GM defines the check precisely: channel E must change in step with the average cell voltage, and a stuck reading in 35 of 40 samples sets the code, Type A; the 2012 two-mode hybrids instead flag block 5 when 20 times its value differs from the pack voltage by over 70 V. Open, low and high faults are separate codes.

causes.label: Battery pack control module software, fixed by reflash (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Channel E reading frozen in the measuring chip
Block voltage measurement drifting from pack voltage (GM two-mode)

symptoms: MIL on
Scheduled charging does not start
Premature oil change or fuel refresh message (Pacifica)

P0B51.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit Low
P0B51.description: P0B51 tells that cell sense channel E reads near zero. GM's battery energy control module only runs this check under clear conditions: the module is in run, crank or accessory mode, the second protection self-test is not running, and no slave communication, open sense line, balancing or internal performance fault is active. Then a reading of 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s in a 2 s window sets the code, Type A, one trip. The order matters for diagnosis: an open sense line or a lost slave board would be reported first by their own codes. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids channel E is block 5, set when blocks 5 and 6 both drop below 2 V, Type B. Electric operation is then restricted.

causes.label: Channel E sense line shorted to its neighbour
Faulty input on the cell monitoring slave board
Pin backed out of the monitoring harness connector

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning
Electric-only driving unavailable

P0B52.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit High
P0B52.description: The threshold behind P0B52 is chosen so that only a measurement error can reach it. A lithium-ion cell is fully charged at roughly 4.2 V, yet GM's battery energy control module waits for 4.8 V or more on channel E, for 1.4 s within 2 s, before storing the code as Type A, one trip. On the nickel-metal hydride packs of the 2012 two-mode trucks and SUVs the corresponding limit is 23 V for block 5, confirmed in 15 of 20 samples and stored as Type B. Since a false high reading could make the controller stop charging early or misjudge balancing, power and charging are restricted. Real overvoltage of a cell is reported by its own cell voltage codes.

causes.label: Channel E sense line contacting a higher cell tap
Faulty measuring input or reference in the monitoring module

symptoms: Charging stops early or is refused
MIL and reduced battery power
Shorter electric range

P0B53.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B53.description: P0B53 belongs to cell sense channel E and describes a signal that is sometimes fine and sometimes not. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM, for example, covers channel E with open, range, low and high tests but publishes no erratic test, so the meaning rests on the J2012 wording and on CARB's rule that every voltage sensor of the energy storage system must be monitored. For the workshop the useful evidence is the freeze frame plus a recorded drive: brief steps in cell voltage E that no other channel shares point to a contact problem on that one path. The driver sees warnings that clear and return, sometimes with a short loss of electric power.

causes.label: Intermittent contact at the channel E tap or connector
Chafed sense lead touching briefly under movement
Marginal component on the monitoring board

symptoms: Warning that clears and returns
Brief loss of electric power while driving

P0B54.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit
P0B54.description: Ford's 2024 special service message for the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit is the most instructive case for P0B54: vehicles built up to 9 December 2023 could store this and the other open-line codes from P0B3B to P0B5E, show the wrench light, refuse to start or charge, or display Stop Safely Now, and the cause was an intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit cable rather than the cells. The 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV shows the same code with a battery replacement as remedy. P0B54 itself means sense channel F is electrically open; GM confirms this with neighbouring cells at least 1.3 V apart, a balanced cell under 36 mV or a splice above 0.1 V for 0.6 s, Type A.

causes.label: Intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit cable (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit built to Dec 2023)
Open channel F tap or splice
Internal traction battery failure (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: Powertrain malfunction (wrench) indicator on
No start or no charging
Stop Safely Now message

P0B55.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit Range/Performance
P0B55.description: P0B55 is the plausibility code of cell channel F: the signal exists and lies inside its range, yet it does not move like the rest of the pack. On the 2016 Chevrolet Volt the vehicle integration control module checks whether channel F moves in the same direction as the average cell voltage, failing it after 7 seconds in an 8 second window, Type A; GM's 2019 tables use 35 failures in 40 samples of 100 ms. The 2012 two-mode hybrids compare block 6, times 20, with the pack voltage and allow 70 V. Chrysler labels it Voltage Sense 6 Circuit Performance on the 2020 Pacifica PHEV, the highest channel in that bulletin, and resolves it with BPCM software.

causes.label: Battery controller software, fixed by update (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV)
Channel F measuring input stuck or slow to respond
Increased resistance in the channel F tap or connector

symptoms: MIL with otherwise normal driving
Reduced hybrid or electric performance

P0B56.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit Low
P0B56.description: The GM two-mode hybrids of 2012, Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra, show a detail of P0B56 that lithium-ion packs lack. Their nickel-metal hydride pack is read in blocks, channel F being block 6, and the battery pack control module sets the code only when block 6 and block 7 both read under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms, Type B, two trips; a shared sense wire between the blocks is the obvious suspect then. In GM's lithium-ion systems the battery energy control module uses 0.2 V or less on cell voltage F for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A. In both cases the controller assumes a failed measurement and reduces battery use until repair.

causes.label: Fault in the sense wire shared by blocks 6 and 7 (GM two-mode)
Channel F sense line shorted to a neighbouring line
Failed input on the cell monitoring electronics

symptoms: Hybrid system warning, MIL after the second drive (two-mode)
Engine runs continuously, no electric launch
Lower fuel economy

P0B57.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit High
P0B57.description: P0B57 stands for an implausibly high value on cell sense channel F, as opposed to P0B56 for an implausibly low one and P0B55 for a frozen value. GM uses fixed upper limits: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s in the battery energy control module of its lithium-ion systems (Type A, one trip), and above 23 V for block 6 in the 2012 two-mode trucks (15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips). Both values lie clearly above what the cell or block can physically reach, so a real overcharge is not the explanation. Look for a sense lead in contact with a higher potential or for a measuring fault inside the module, and expect limited battery power and charging until then.

causes.label: Channel F sense lead touching a higher potential
Measuring input or reference fault in the module

symptoms: MIL and battery warning
Battery charging limited
Weaker acceleration in hybrid mode

P0B58.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense F Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B58.description: P0B58 is reserved for an erratic signal on cell sense channel F, and the honest state is short: no manufacturer documents this code publicly. The neighbouring codes are well covered; Ford and GM use the open circuit code P0B54, GM and Chrysler the range code P0B55, GM the fixed low and high limits. CARB demands monitoring of all battery voltage sensors of the storage system. An erratic test would catch sudden steps between successive samples that stay inside the low and high limits. Likely causes are a sense tap that loosens under vibration or a damaged section of the flexible circuit, and the symptoms typically come and go with road conditions and temperature.

causes.label: Sense tap of channel F loosening under vibration
Damaged section of the flexible sense circuit

symptoms: Sporadic warning depending on road or temperature
Occasional brief power reduction

P0B59.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit
P0B59.description: Voltage sense G is the seventh cell measuring channel; how many cells or groups it covers depends on how the manufacturer splits the pack among monitoring chips. P0B59 is its open-circuit code. Two Ford bulletins name it: the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV, where the open-line group up to P0B7C leads to a battery replacement, and the 2023 Mach-E and E-Transit, where it is blamed on the BECM flexible printed circuit. GM's BECM sets it after 0.6 s of an open-line pattern such as adjacent cells 1.3 V apart, a balanced cell under 36 mV or splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V, Type A. If several channels report at once, suspect a shared connection first.

causes.label: Open channel G tap, splice or bus bar contact
Intermittent BECM flexible circuit (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit)
Internal traction battery failure (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: Vehicle not ready to drive
Charging blocked
Wrench light or hybrid warning

P0B5A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit Range/Performance
P0B5A.description: P0B5A asks whether cell channel G behaves like a real cell. GM answers that question in three ways across its programmes. The 2019 hybrid tables expect channel G to trend with the average cell voltage and set the code after 35 frozen samples out of 40, Type A. The 2016 Chevrolet Volt uses a 7 of 8 second window, the Cadillac ELR 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms. The 2012 two-mode trucks compare block 7, multiplied by 20, with the pack voltage and fail it beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B. The Chrysler Pacifica bulletin stops at channel 6, so no other maker is documented for this code. A frozen or drifting measurement input is the most common cause.

causes.label: Channel G measuring input frozen or drifting
Block 7 reading out of line with pack voltage (GM two-mode)
Monitoring software issue, check for updates

symptoms: MIL without obvious drivability change
Limited hybrid assist

P0B5B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit Low
P0B5B.description: When P0B5B appears, the battery controller has seen cell sense channel G at a level no usable cell would show, and it shuts down or restricts electric operation to stay on the safe side. GM documents the trigger for its lithium-ion systems as cell voltage G at or below 0.2 V for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, with the test held off while communication, open line or balancing faults are active. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids channel G is block 7, and the code needs blocks 7 and 8 together under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Sense wiring, connector pins and the monitoring input deserve attention before the cells, which have their own cell voltage codes.

causes.label: Channel G sense line shorted to a neighbouring line
Damaged or backed-out pin in the monitoring connector
Failed measuring input on the monitoring module

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Electric drive disabled or restricted

P0B5C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit High
P0B5C.description: P0B5C marks an out-of-range high reading on cell sense channel G. For a technician the quickest plausibility check is arithmetic: the sum of all cell or block readings should match the pack voltage, so a single channel that reads far too high while the total stays normal is a sensing fault. GM formalises the limits as 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s in the battery energy control module of its lithium-ion systems, Type A, one trip, and as more than 23 V for block 7 of the 2012 two-mode trucks and SUVs, 15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips. Overcharged cells are flagged by other codes. Until the fault is fixed, battery power and charging are limited.

causes.label: Channel G sense lead touching a higher cell tap
Faulty measuring input or reference in the module
Contamination or moisture on the monitoring board

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning
Charging limited or refused

P0B5D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense G Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B5D.description: P0B5D is the J2012 code for an unsteady signal on cell sense channel G, a reading that flickers or drops out for moments without staying beyond a limit. No manufacturer documents P0B5D publicly. For orientation: GM monitors channel G with an open-line test (P0B59), a frozen-value comparison against the average cell voltage (P0B5A) and fixed low and high limits (P0B5B, P0B5C), but lists no erratic monitor. CARB requires the battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system to be monitored and faults to be traced to the smallest replaceable unit. For the owner the result is a warning that may vanish after a restart and reappear later; the root cause is usually a marginal contact.

causes.label: Marginal contact at the channel G tap or connector
Sense harness under strain, losing contact with pack movement

symptoms: Warning that disappears after restart and returns
Brief reduction of electric power

P0B5E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit
P0B5E.description: P0B5E flags a broken measuring path on voltage sense H, the eighth cell tap channel read by the battery monitoring electronics. In GM's 2019 tables the battery energy control module runs an open sense line test within a 0.6 s window: neighbouring cells diverging by 1.3 V or more, a cell under 36 mV while its balancing switch is on, or a splice above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a bus bar splice) sets it as Type A. Ford names P0B5E in two bulletins: a no-start on the 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid, repaired with a new traction battery, and the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit, where H is the last code of the affected range and an intermittent flexible printed circuit at the BECM is blamed. Starting and charging may fail.

causes.label: Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable at the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit 2023)
Open cell tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel H
Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)

symptoms: Powertrain malfunction (wrench) indicator and Stop Safely Now message
Vehicle does not start or does not become ready to drive
High-voltage battery cannot be charged

P0B5F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Range/Performance
P0B5F.description: With P0B5F the channel H wiring is intact, but the value it delivers does not fit the rest of the battery. GM runs two quite different plausibility tests. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids (Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado, Sierra) channel H is nickel-metal hydride block 8 of 20; the battery pack control module multiplies blocks 8 and 9 by twenty and fails the test when both differ from the measured pack voltage by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B, two trips, with active pack voltage codes P0ABB to P0ABD blocking it. Lithium-ion systems in the 2019 tables look for a frozen reading instead: if H stays put while the average cell voltage trends, 35 of 40 samples set the code, Type A.

causes.label: Block or cell voltage input for channel H drifting away from the true value
Measuring chip input stuck at a constant value
Faulty pack voltage reference distorting the comparison

symptoms: Hybrid system warning with MIL
Reduced electric assist or regeneration
Inaccurate state-of-charge display

P0B60.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Low
P0B60.description: P0B60 means channel H reports less voltage than any healthy cell or block could hold, so the measurement itself is suspect. GM publishes three variants. Lithium-ion packs with a battery energy control module (2016 and 2019 tables) trip at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A, provided no open-line, communication or balancing fault is already stored. The BAS Plus mild hybrid in table 13OBDG05C uses a cell sense line threshold of 1.4 V and needs 7 failures out of 10, Type B. The 2012 two-mode trucks compare blocks 8 and 9, both under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Typical culprits are a sense lead shorted to ground or a failed input on the monitoring board.

causes.label: Channel H sense lead shorted to ground or to the next lower tap
Failed measuring input on the cell monitoring board
Cell or block on channel H actually collapsed

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
Electric drive power limited or switched off
Charging interrupted

P0B61.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit High
P0B61.description: A lithium-ion cell cannot sit much above about 4.2 V, so when channel H reads 4.8 V or more the GM battery energy control module concludes the sense circuit is wrong and stores P0B61 after 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid sets the same code at more than 4.65 V on the cell sense line in 7 of 10 samples, Type B, while the 2012 two-mode hybrids treat H as nickel-metal hydride block 8 and only object above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. A high reading usually comes from a sense lead touching a higher potential or from a monitoring input that floats when a reference connection is lost. Unlike P0B60 the controller here suspects overvoltage, so charging is typically blocked.

causes.label: Channel H sense lead in contact with a higher cell tap
Lost reference connection letting the measuring input float
Internal fault of the cell monitoring chip

symptoms: Charging refused or stopped early
MIL with reduced electric power

P0B62.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B62.description: P0B62 describes a channel H signal that jumps or cuts out for moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
