It is worth noting that Ford's 2023 Mach-E and E-Transit bulletin attributes an intermittent flexible printed circuit fault to the open-circuit code P0B5E, not to P0B62, and GM's published tables contain no erratic monitor for channel H at all. The code is therefore defined by SAE J2012 but appears to remain unused in practice. CARB demands that battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system be checked like every other input. If it ever appears, logging channel H next to channels G and I while moving the harness is the sensible first step.

causes.label: Intermittent contact at the channel H connector or flexible circuit
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board
Inverter noise coupling into the sense line

symptoms: Warning appears occasionally and clears after a restart
Short interruptions of electric drive

P0B63.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit
P0B63.description: Channel I is the ninth sense input of the battery monitoring chain, and P0B63 reports that its circuit is open. GM shows how differently this can be detected. The BAS Plus mild hybrid (table 13OBDG05C) watches the voltage of line N and its neighbour N-1: if both drop under 1.4 V and change by more than 0.5 V within 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples set the code, Type B. The newer battery energy control module of the 2019 tables relies on neighbouring cells drifting 1.3 V apart, a balancing test below 36 mV or a splice voltage, all within 0.6 s, Type A. Ford lists P0B63 among the open-line codes behind a no-start on the 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid and replaces the traction battery.

causes.label: Broken channel I sense wire, crimp or cell tap
Internal traction battery fault, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Corroded or loose connector at the cell monitoring board

symptoms: Vehicle will not start or enter ready mode
Service hybrid or EV system warning
Electric mode unavailable

P0B64.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Range/Performance
P0B64.description: P0B64 is a rationality fault: channel I is connected and reads a believable number, yet it does not move with the other cells. GM's 2016 Chevrolet Volt compares the movement of each cell with the average; if channel I does not follow when the average moves by more than 0.022 V, 7 out of 8 seconds fail the check, Type A. The 2019 hybrid powertrain control processor 2 tables keep the idea but count samples, 35 failures out of 40 at 100 ms. On the 2012 two-mode trucks the same code belongs to nickel-metal hydride block 9, whose scaled value must stay within 70 V of the pack voltage. Because the input is alive but stuck or drifting, a software update or the monitoring board is a likelier fix than wiring.

causes.label: Channel I measuring input frozen at a constant value
Battery controller software misjudging the channel
High-resistance cell tap damping the signal

symptoms: MIL on, vehicle drives normally
Reduced hybrid assist or electric range

P0B65.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Low
P0B65.description: The 2012 GM two-mode hybrids show a detail worth knowing for P0B65: their battery pack control module only declares channel I, nickel-metal hydride block 9, too low when block 9 and its neighbour block 10 both read under 2 V, and only after 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms; the fault is Type B and needs two trips. A single weak block alone therefore does not set it. GM's lithium-ion controllers judge each cell on its own, setting P0B65 at 0.2 V or less held for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, as long as no open-line or communication fault has priority. The BAS Plus mild hybrid uses 1.4 V and 7 of 10 samples. In all cases the reading is too low to be a real cell.

causes.label: Channel I sense lead shorted to ground or a lower tap
Connector fault affecting adjacent blocks 9 and 10 (two-mode)
Failed measuring input in the battery controller

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Engine runs more often, electric assist reduced
Limited power in limp mode

P0B66.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit High
P0B66.description: When channel I claims a voltage above what its cell or block can physically reach, the controller stores P0B66. The thresholds GM publishes depend on chemistry and architecture: lithium-ion packs with a battery energy control module set it at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; the BAS Plus mild hybrid at above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B; the 2012 two-mode trucks, which measure nickel-metal hydride block 9 rather than single cells, above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Every limit sits clearly above normal full charge, so a real overcharged cell is unlikely. Look first for a sense lead touching the next tap up or for a measuring input that has lost its reference.

causes.label: Channel I lead touching a higher-potential tap
Open reference or ground of the measuring chip
Genuinely overcharged cell after a charging control fault

symptoms: Charging stops or is refused
MIL and reduced power

P0B67.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B67.description: SAE J2012 reserves P0B67 for an unsteady signal on channel I, meaning readings that spike, drop and recover. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the GM tables that define the other four channel I codes includes an erratic test. The fault picture would sit between an open circuit (P0B63) and a frozen value (P0B64): the line works most of the time but loses contact under vibration, heat or current load. CARB requires battery voltage sensors to be monitored as inputs of the energy storage system, which explains why the code exists at all. For diagnosis, record cell voltage I with a scan tool during a drive and compare its noise with neighbouring channels H and J.

causes.label: Sense contact on channel I opening under vibration or heat
Corroded terminal in the module connector

symptoms: Sporadic warning without a reproducible pattern
Momentary drop in electric power

P0B68.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit
P0B68.description: For owners of a 2019 or 2020 Ford Fusion plug-in hybrid, P0B68 is best known from bulletin 23-2039: the car will not start, the battery energy control module stores one or more open sense line codes from P0B3B to P0B7C, and the prescribed repair is a complete high-voltage traction battery. Technically the code says that the tenth measuring channel, J, has lost its connection to the cells. GM describes the test in detail for its lithium-ion packs: within 0.6 s it looks for adjacent cells 1.3 V apart, a cell under 36 mV while being balanced, or splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V, and sets P0B68 as Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid uses a 1.4 V and 0.5 V rate-of-change test, Type B.

causes.label: Internal traction battery failure, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV 2019-2020)
Open sense wire or cell tap on channel J
Bad bus bar or splice connection near channel J

symptoms: No start, vehicle does not become ready
Hybrid system warning on the cluster
Plug-in charging unavailable

P0B69.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Range/Performance
P0B69.description: P0B69 is set when channel J is electrically present but its readings do not behave plausibly. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid explains the logic most clearly: once the average cell voltage moves by more than 0.045 V, the cell under test must move in the same direction and by at least half as much; 20 failures in 40 samples set the code as Type B, two trips. The 2019 lithium-ion tables use a tighter trigger of 0.022 V and 35 of 40 samples, Type A. On the 2012 two-mode trucks the code belongs to nickel-metal hydride block 10 and compares its scaled value with the pack voltage. Neither Ford nor Chrysler publishes this channel; Chrysler's Pacifica bulletin stops at sense 6.

causes.label: Channel J input reacting too little to real voltage changes
Corroded or high-resistance cell tap
Calibration error in the battery controller

symptoms: MIL without obvious driveability problem
Hybrid assist reduced

P0B6A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Low
P0B6A.description: A reading of almost zero on channel J points to the measurement, not to the cell, and that is what P0B6A records. In GM's lithium-ion systems (2016 and 2019 tables) the battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A. The interesting part is what it ignores: while a module communication loss, an open sense line code, a balancing fault or an internal module fault is active, P0B6A stays silent so that the root cause is stored first. The 2012 two-mode hybrids look at nickel-metal hydride block 10 together with block 11, both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Expect reduced or no electric drive until the circuit is repaired.

causes.label: Channel J lead chafed through and shorted to ground
Damaged measuring input on the monitoring board
Cell on channel J internally shorted

symptoms: Electric drive limited or unavailable
MIL and battery warning message

P0B6B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit High
P0B6B.description: On GM's 2012 two-mode hybrid trucks the battery is divided into 20 nickel-metal hydride blocks, and channel J is block 10. The battery pack control module samples it every 100 ms while the 12 V supply is between 9 and 18 V; if block 10 reports more than 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, P0B6B is stored as Type B, so the MIL comes on after the second trip. Lithium-ion GM packs check single cells instead and set the code at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A; the BAS Plus mild hybrid uses 4.65 V. Since these limits lie well above any real charge level, a wiring short to a higher tap or a faulty sense input is the expected finding, not an overcharged battery.

causes.label: Channel J lead shorted to a higher block or cell tap
Faulty measuring input in the battery pack control module

symptoms: MIL after the second drive (Type B systems)
Charging or regeneration restricted
Reduced electric power

P0B6C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B6C.description: No manufacturer documents P0B6C publicly. The code stands for a channel J signal that is unstable, with brief jumps or dropouts, as opposed to the steady faults covered by P0B68 to P0B6B. CARB section 1968.2 requires that the individual electronic inputs of a hybrid energy storage system, battery voltage sensors expressly included, be monitored for circuit and rationality faults; erratic behaviour is one way such a fault can show. GM, which publishes tests for the other four channel J codes, lists none for this one. For the driver it would mean a warning that comes and goes, possibly with short power cuts. A cable or connector with marginal contact is the most plausible cause.

causes.label: Marginal contact in the channel J harness or connector
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring electronics

symptoms: Intermittent warning light
Brief power reductions while driving

P0B6D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit
P0B6D.description: P0B6D marks an open circuit on voltage sense K, the eleventh cell measuring channel. GM has used the code since its first published hybrid tables: in 2011 the open-line test already checked bus bar voltages, flagging more than 0.7 V. The 2019 battery energy control module refines it into seven cases, among them adjacent cells 1.3 V apart, a cell under 36 mV with balancing active and splice voltages over 0.1 V, all judged in a 0.6 s window and set as Type A. Ford counts P0B6D among the open sense line codes that leave a 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid unable to start and fixes it by replacing the traction battery. Before any pack work, the high-voltage system has to be disabled by trained staff.

causes.label: Loose or corroded bus bar connection at the channel K tap
Internal traction battery fault, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
Broken sense wire between cells and monitoring board

symptoms: Vehicle not ready to drive
Hybrid or EV system warning with MIL
Charging not possible

P0B6E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Range/Performance
P0B6E.description: In a nickel-metal hydride pack with 20 equal blocks, twenty times one block voltage should roughly equal the whole pack voltage. GM's 2012 two-mode hybrids use exactly this for P0B6E, assigned to block 11: the battery pack control module checks blocks 11 and 12, and if both scaled values deviate from the pack voltage sensor by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, the code is set, Type B. The test only runs with the contactors closed for over 200 ms and no pack voltage fault active. GM's lithium-ion controllers judge channel K differently, as a frozen value that fails to follow the average cell voltage (35 of 40 samples, Type A, in the 2019 tables). No other manufacturer publishes it.

causes.label: Block or cell voltage measurement of channel K out of calibration
Pack voltage sensor reading off, distorting the comparison
Measuring input stuck at one value

symptoms: MIL after two trips
Less electric assist, more engine running

P0B6F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Low
P0B6F.description: GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid, the eAssist system in table 13OBDG05C, gives P0B6F a simple rule: if the cell sense line for channel K measures below 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples at 200 ms while the 12 V supply is above 8.8 V, the code is stored as Type B, two trips. Since a lithium-ion cell in use never falls that low, the value must come from a short or a failed input. GM's later battery energy control modules work with 0.2 V and a 1.4 s window, Type A, and the 2012 two-mode trucks with nickel-metal hydride blocks 11 and 12, both under 2 V. The driver typically sees a hybrid warning and loses electric assist; the engine takes over more of the work.

causes.label: Channel K sense line shorted to ground or a lower tap
Failed measuring input in the battery interface module
Blown protective element in the sense line

symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL after the second trip
Auto stop and electric assist disabled

P0B70.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit High
P0B70.description: P0B70 says that cell voltage K reads too high to be genuine. GM's 2019 battery energy control module sets it at 4.8 V or more, held for 1.4 s within 2 s, as a Type A fault with immediate MIL, and only when no communication loss, open sense line or internal module fault takes precedence. The same principle appears with other numbers elsewhere at GM: 4.65 V and 7 of 10 samples on the BAS Plus mild hybrid, 23 V for nickel-metal hydride block 11 on the 2012 two-mode trucks. The difference to P0B6F is the direction, not the location: a high reading typically comes from a lead touching a higher potential, a low one from a short to a lower one. Charging is usually blocked while it is active.

causes.label: Channel K lead in contact with a higher tap
Floating measuring input after loss of its lower reference
Cell monitoring chip fault

symptoms: Charging blocked
MIL and power limitation

P0B71.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B71.description: P0B71 belongs to the unsteady fault type: the channel K reading flickers or drops out momentarily without staying beyond a fixed limit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Neither GM's hybrid tables from 2011 to 2019 nor the Ford and Chrysler bulletins on cell sense codes mention it, although they cover the open, plausibility, low and high codes of neighbouring channels. Its basis is the CARB requirement to monitor battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system as input components. In a workshop the approach would be a wiggle test on the module harness while watching cell voltage K live, plus a check of the connector terminals for fretting corrosion.

causes.label: Fretting corrosion on channel K connector terminals
Sense harness under strain losing contact with movement

symptoms: Warning that comes and goes
Occasional short loss of electric power

P0B72.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit
P0B72.description: P0B72 reports an open circuit on voltage sense L, the twelfth channel. One detail sets it apart from its neighbours: GM's 2011 hybrid tables list every open sense line code from P0B3B upward except P0B72 (and P0B90), so the early system did not use it, while L's range, low and high codes were present. Later GM tables include it. The BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it when lines N and N-1 fall below 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B; the 2019 battery energy control module uses its adjacent-cell, balancing and splice tests within 0.6 s, Type A. Ford's Fusion plug-in hybrid bulletin for 2019-2020 includes P0B72 and replaces the traction battery.

causes.label: Open sense lead, crimp or cell tap on channel L
Internal traction battery failure, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV)
High-resistance splice or bus bar joint

symptoms: No start or no ready mode
Battery or hybrid system warning
Charging aborted

P0B73.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Range/Performance
P0B73.description: Channel L delivers a value, but P0B73 tells you that the value is not credible. GM checks this in three ways. The 2016 Chevrolet Volt and the 2019 lithium-ion systems test whether cell L moves in the same direction as the average once that average changes by more than 0.022 V, failing 7 of 8 seconds or 35 of 40 samples respectively, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid demands at least half of the average movement, 20 of 40 samples, Type B. The 2012 two-mode trucks treat L as nickel-metal hydride block 12 and compare blocks 12 and 13, scaled by twenty, with the pack voltage, failing beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B. A battery controller reflash or measuring board repair is the usual remedy.

causes.label: Channel L input not following real cell voltage changes
Battery controller software or calibration issue
Corroded cell tap slowing the signal

symptoms: MIL with normal driving behaviour
Reduced electric range or assist

P0B74.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Low
P0B74.description: P0B74 is set when channel L reads implausibly low. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids, where L is nickel-metal hydride block 12 of 20, the battery pack control module needs both block 12 and block 13 under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples before it stores the code as Type B; no battery control module fault P0A1F may be active. For lithium-ion packs GM's 2016 and 2019 tables use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, and the BAS Plus mild hybrid 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. A short of the sense lead to a lower potential, a defective monitoring input or, more rarely, a cell that has really collapsed are the candidates. The vehicle will normally restrict electric operation.

causes.label: Channel L sense lead shorted to a lower potential
Defective measuring input in the battery controller
Cell or block on channel L actually failed

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning
Electric operation restricted
Engine runs continuously on hybrids

P0B75.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit High
P0B75.description: With P0B75 the battery controller rejects channel L because it reads above any value a real cell or block can reach. GM's lithium-ion systems in the 2016 Volt and the 2019 tables set it at 4.8 V or more over 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid at above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. On the 2012 two-mode trucks, block 12 must exceed 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, sampled every 100 ms, before the code is stored as Type B. The pairing with P0B74 helps diagnosis: low points to a short downward, high to contact with a higher tap or a floating input. While it is active, charging and regeneration are normally limited to protect the pack.

causes.label: Channel L lead touching a higher tap
Floating measuring input after an open reference line
Real overvoltage of the cell after a charging fault

symptoms: Charging and regeneration limited
MIL and hybrid or EV warning

P0B76.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B76.description: P0B76 closes the channel L group and covers an erratic signal: values that jump or vanish briefly while the circuit otherwise works. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, the only maker with public tables for L, defines open, plausibility, low and high tests for this channel but no erratic test, and the Ford bulletins name only the open-circuit code P0B72. CARB obliges manufacturers to monitor the battery voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system, which is the regulatory background of the code. Practically, an intermittent contact at the channel L tap, a fatigued harness or a cracked board joint would produce this picture. Warnings may disappear after a restart and return.

causes.label: Intermittent contact at the channel L cell tap
Fatigued sense harness wire
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board

symptoms: Warning clears after restart and comes back
Momentary power reduction

P0B77.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit
P0B77.description: P0B77 flags an open or high-resistance tap on voltage sense M, the thirteenth cell channel. GM's 2019 battery energy control module checks seven cases: adjacent cells differing by 1.3 V or more, a balancing gate reading below 36 mV, or splice voltages above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a busbar splice). M is the last channel there with the short 0.6 s window, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid instead needs lines N and N-1 both below 1.4 V plus a jump over 0.5 V within 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. Ford's TSB 23-2039 names P0B77 for 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids that no longer start and prescribes a new traction battery. Range, low and high faults on M carry their own codes.

causes.label: Open or corroded tap of sense lead M at the cell connector
Fault inside the traction battery (Ford Fusion PHEV TSB 23-2039)
High resistance at a splice or busbar joint in the sense path
Defective cell monitoring board input

symptoms: MIL with hybrid or EV system warning
Vehicle may not start or go into ready mode
Charging blocked or limited

P0B78.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Range/Performance
P0B78.description: With P0B78 the controller doubts the reading of channel M rather than its wiring. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain processor watches for a frozen value: whenever the average of all cells moves by more than 0.022 V, cell M must follow by at least 0.005 V in the same direction, and 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set a Type A fault. The 2012 two-mode trucks map M to nickel-metal hydride block 13 and multiply blocks 13 and 14 by twenty; if that estimate misses the pack voltage by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, the code is stored as Type B. The BAS Plus mild hybrid wants at least half the average movement, 20 of 40 samples, Type B. A plausible but wrong value is often a controller or measuring board issue.

causes.label: Measuring channel M stuck at a fixed value
Battery controller software needing an update
Block 13 voltage drifting from the pack on two-mode NiMH packs

symptoms: MIL on, often without noticeable driving change
Reduced electric assist or regeneration

P0B79.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Low
P0B79.description: P0B79 means that the voltage reported for sense M is too low to be real. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 set it at 0.2 V or less, held for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A, and only while no open sense line fault is active, so a broken lead is reported by P0B77 first. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids M is block 13: the battery pack control module needs block 13 and block 14 both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. The BAS Plus mild hybrid uses 1.4 V, 7 of 10 samples, with the 12 V supply above 8.8 V. Typical sources are a sense lead shorted towards ground or a lower cell, a failed measuring input, or rarely a cell that has truly collapsed.

causes.label: Sense lead M shorted to ground or a lower cell potential
Failed measuring input on the monitoring board
Cell or NiMH block on channel M actually collapsed

symptoms: MIL and service hybrid or EV system message
Electric drive or assist disabled
Engine runs continuously on hybrids

P0B7A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit High
P0B7A.description: A reading on channel M above what any healthy cell can deliver produces P0B7A. For lithium-ion packs GM sets the line at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window and treats it as Type A, illuminating the MIL on the first trip. The BAS Plus mild hybrid already reacts above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. Where M stands for NiMH block 13, as on the 2012 two-mode trucks, a block voltage above 23 V for 15 of 20 samples is the trigger, again Type B, with the 12 V system between 9 and 18 V. Because a cell itself rarely climbs that high, a sense lead touching a higher potential or a faulty measuring input is far more likely than overcharging. The vehicle will usually limit charging and electric drive.

causes.label: Sense lead M in contact with a higher cell potential
Measuring input of channel M reading high
Real overvoltage of the cell after a balancing fault

symptoms: MIL on from the first trip (GM lithium-ion, Type A)
Charging stopped or limited
Reduced electric power

P0B7B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B7B.description: P0B7B is reserved for a sense M signal that flickers: short dropouts or jumps while the circuit is otherwise intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's tables for channel M contain open, plausibility, low and high tests but no erratic test, and Ford's Fusion bulletin lists only the open-circuit code P0B77. The legal footing is CARB 1968.2, which requires the battery voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system to be monitored as electronic components and demands fault codes that point to the smallest replaceable unit. In practice a loose crimp at the M tap, a chafed lead in the sense harness or a cracked solder joint on the monitoring board would cause such a signal. Expect warnings that come and go.

causes.label: Loose crimp or connector at the channel M tap
Chafed wire in the cell sense harness
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board

symptoms: Hybrid warning appearing and clearing again
Brief drops in electric power

P0B7C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit
P0B7C.description: Voltage sense N, the fourteenth channel, reports a broken or high-resistance sense lead with P0B7C. It is the last code in Ford's TSB 23-2039: 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids that fail to start with any open-circuit code from P0B3B up to P0B7C get a replacement traction battery; the bulletin names no channel beyond N. In GM's 2019 battery controller tables N is the first channel whose open test runs 0.8 s within a 1.6 s window instead of 0.6 s, while the criteria (1.3 V adjacent-cell difference, 36 mV balancing gate, splice limits) stay the same, Type A. A second GM program of 2016 closes the balancing gates in a test pattern, turns the voltage drop into a sense-line resistance and fails above 30.00 in 7 of 9 samples, Type A.

causes.label: Internal traction battery fault (Ford Fusion PHEV 2019-2020)
Sense lead N broken or with excessive resistance
Fault on the cell monitoring board

symptoms: No start or vehicle does not become ready
MIL and stop-safely or service message
Plug-in charging unavailable

P0B7D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Range/Performance
P0B7D.description: P0B7D concerns a channel N value that stays inside its limits yet does not behave like a real cell. GM's 2016 tables show how the same check is tuned per vehicle: the Chevrolet Volt fails when cell N does not move with the average for 7 of 8 seconds, while the Cadillac ELR counts 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms once the average shifts by more than 0.006 V; both are Type A. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids N corresponds to NiMH block 14, and blocks 14 and 15 scaled by twenty must agree with the pack voltage within 70 V, otherwise 160 of 170 samples set a Type B code. The 2019 processor uses its 0.005 V trend test, 35 of 40 samples. Often a battery controller reflash or a board repair is the fix.

causes.label: Channel N value not tracking the other cells
Outdated battery controller calibration
Block 14 or 15 voltage mismatch on two-mode NiMH packs

symptoms: MIL with hybrid service message
Shorter electric range or less assist

P0B7E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Low
P0B7E.description: P0B7E sets when channel N reads below the lower plausibility limit. GM's 2016 program with a separate battery sense module uses less than 0.20 V and needs 14 failures in 18 samples, about 1.8 s at 100 ms each, before a Type A fault; the open-circuit test must not be failing at the same time. The other GM lithium-ion controllers use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s in 2 s, also Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid works with 1.4 V and 7 of 10 samples, Type B. On 2012 two-mode trucks N is NiMH block 14, and blocks 14 and 15 must both drop under 2 V. A low reading usually comes from the measuring path, not from the cell: a lead shorted to a lower potential or a damaged input stage.

causes.label: Sense lead N shorted to a lower potential
Damaged input stage in the sense module
Deeply discharged or failed cell on channel N

symptoms: MIL from the first trip on lithium-ion GM systems
Hybrid system limits power
Combustion engine does not shut off at standstill

P0B7F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit High
P0B7F.description: Channel N reporting more voltage than a cell can hold leads to P0B7F. GM uses three thresholds depending on the system: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in 2 s on most lithium-ion battery controllers, above 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples on the 2016 program with a separate sense module, both Type A, and above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples on the BAS Plus mild hybrid, Type B. The 2012 two-mode trucks treat N as NiMH block 14 and set the code above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. The low counterpart is P0B7E, an open lead is P0B7C. Before suspecting the cell, a technician checks whether the N lead touches a neighbouring higher potential or whether the measuring input has drifted.

causes.label: Sense lead N touching a higher potential
Drifted measuring input in the battery controller
Real overvoltage of the cell on channel N

symptoms: MIL and warning in the instrument cluster
Regenerative braking and charging limited

P0B80.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B80.description: P0B80 describes an unsteady channel N signal: the voltage drops out or jumps for moments, then looks normal again. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford's Fusion plug-in bulletin, which reaches exactly up to channel N, cites only the open-circuit code P0B7C, and GM's tables give channel N open, rationality, low and high diagnostics without a separate erratic test. Background is CARB 1968.2, under which battery voltage sensors in a hybrid energy storage system count as monitored components with their own fault codes. If a vehicle does store it, the trigger would be a contact that opens under vibration or temperature change, for example at the N tap, in the harness connector or at a board joint. Restarting may hide the fault for a while.

causes.label: Contact at the N tap opening under vibration
Fretting corrosion in the sense harness connector
Solder joint cracking with temperature cycles

symptoms: Intermittent hybrid warning
Fault not present after restart
Occasional loss of electric power

P0B81.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit
P0B81.description: P0B81 stands for an open sense lead on channel O, the fifteenth cell tap. GM has used it from the start: the 2011 Volt battery tables already list P0B81 among the open sense line codes and detect, among other cases, a busbar connection voltage above 0.7 V. In the 2019 battery energy control module the test needs 0.8 s within a 1.6 s window, with adjacent cells 1.3 V or more apart or a balancing gate below 36 mV, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid compares lines N and N-1, both under 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. Unlike channels M and N, P0B81 does not appear in Ford's Fusion plug-in bulletin. With the lead open, the controller loses sight of that cell and limits operation.

causes.label: Loose or high-resistance busbar joint at the O tap
Broken sense wire O in the battery harness
Faulty cell sense module

symptoms: MIL and propulsion system warning
Reduced power or no electric drive

P0B82.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Range/Performance
P0B82.description: P0B82 is a plausibility verdict on channel O. GM's 2016 program with a battery sense module asks cell O to trend at least 0.002 V in the direction of the average whenever the average moves by more than 0.022 V; 35 failed evaluations out of 40 set a Type A code. The 2019 controllers use the same logic with 0.005 V. Where O is NiMH block 15, on the 2012 two-mode hybrids, the battery pack control module multiplies blocks 15 and 16 by twenty and compares the result with the pack voltage, failing beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B. The BAS Plus mild hybrid needs half the average movement, 20 of 40, Type B. Low, high and open faults on the same channel are reported separately as P0B83, P0B84 and P0B81.

causes.label: Channel O reading frozen in the monitoring electronics
Battery controller software fault
Rising resistance in the O sense tap distorting the reading

symptoms: MIL with otherwise normal driving
State of charge display jumps or is inaccurate

P0B83.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Low
P0B83.description: P0B83 reports that channel O reads implausibly low. It is not the same as an open lead: GM's lithium-ion controllers run this check only while no open sense line fault is present, so a broken wire shows as P0B81 instead. The low limit there is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it below 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. On the 2012 two-mode trucks, where O is NiMH block 15, block 15 and block 16 must both be under 2 V for 15 of 20 samples, Type B, with the 12 V supply between 9 and 18 V. Short circuits in the sense path towards ground or a lower cell are the main suspects; a genuinely dead cell is the exception and usually brings neighbouring codes as well.

causes.label: Short in the O sense path towards ground or a lower cell
Monitoring input reading low
Dead cell or NiMH block 15

symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning lamp
Electric operation switched off

P0B84.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit High
P0B84.description: P0B84 is stored when channel O sits above the upper limit of a credible cell voltage. For GM lithium-ion packs that limit is 4.8 V, held 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A; the 2016 program with a separate sense module tolerates up to 4.90 V and counts 14 failures in 18 samples, also Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid uses a lower ceiling of 4.65 V and a Type B rating. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids the reading belongs to NiMH block 15, which must exceed 23 V in 15 of 20 samples. For the driver the effect is a warning and a battery that is no longer charged fully or used for electric drive. Since true overvoltage is rare, the measuring lead and the input of the monitoring electronics are checked first.

causes.label: Sense lead O shorted to a higher cell tap
Monitoring input of channel O reading too high
Cell overcharged because balancing failed

symptoms: MIL and battery warning
Charging ends early
Less electric assist

P0B85.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B85.description: P0B85 would mark a channel O signal that is present but unsteady, with spikes or brief gaps. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; even GM, whose public tables cover channel O in detail from 2011 onward, defines only the open, rationality, low and high tests for it. The requirement behind the code family comes from CARB 1968.2: voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system must be monitored like other electronic components, with fault codes that identify the part to replace. A plausible cause for such a signal is a contact resistance that changes with movement, heat or moisture, typically at the cell tap, the busbar screw or the connector of the sense harness. A fault that vanishes and returns calls for wiggle testing with live data.

causes.label: Loose busbar screw changing contact resistance at tap O
Moisture or corrosion in the sense harness connector
Cracked joint on the monitoring board

symptoms: Warning that comes and goes
Short-term power reduction during driving

P0B86.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit
P0B86.description: P0B86 belongs to channel P, the sixteenth sense lead, and indicates that this lead has lost its connection to the cell. Comparing GM's tables shows how the timing evolved: the 2016 Volt battery controller decides within 0.6 s, the 2019 version waits 0.8 s in a 1.6 s window; both use the 1.3 V adjacent-cell, 36 mV balancing gate and splice criteria and are Type A. GM's 2016 program with a separate sense module measures the sense line resistance instead, failing above 30.00 in 7 of 9 samples. On the BAS Plus mild hybrid the code is Type B after 7 of 10 samples showing lines N and N-1 below 1.4 V with a step over 0.5 V. Ford's public bulletins do not list P0B86. The pack usually has to come out for repair.

causes.label: Sense lead P open at the cell tap or connector
Excessive resistance in the sense line (corrosion, loose screw)
Defective input of the sense module

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system fault message
Vehicle runs only on the engine or with reduced power

P0B87.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Range/Performance
P0B87.description: P0B87 says channel P is delivering numbers that do not fit the rest of the battery. On GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid the cell under test must move at least 50 percent as far as the average cell voltage; if not, 20 failures in 40 samples set the code as Type B, i.e. MIL after two trips. GM's 2019 lithium-ion processor is stricter in its rating, Type A after 35 of 40 samples, and looks for a value that stays flat by less than 0.005 V while the average moves more than 0.022 V. The 2012 two-mode trucks check NiMH block 16, together with block 17, against the pack voltage with a 70 V window, 160 of 170 samples, Type B. Since wiring faults have their own codes (P0B86, P0B88, P0B89), this one points towards measuring electronics or software.

causes.label: Measuring electronics for channel P out of tolerance
Software or calibration of the battery controller
NiMH block 16 or 17 out of balance with the pack

symptoms: MIL after two trips on Type B systems
Engine start-stop or electric assist less frequent

P0B88.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Low
P0B88.description: A too-low value on sense P, the sixteenth channel, is what P0B88 records. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it at a cell sense line below 1.4 V for 7 of 10 samples, sampled every 200 ms and only with the 12 V battery above 8.8 V; it rates the fault Type B. The full lithium-ion systems in GM's 2016 and 2019 tables react at 0.2 V or less after 1.4 s in a 2 s window and set it as Type A. In the 2012 two-mode NiMH pack, P is block 16; blocks 16 and 17 must both stay below 2 V for 15 of 20 samples. A collapsed reading usually traces back to a short between the P lead and a lower potential, sometimes to a defective input; it is rarely the cell itself. The open-circuit condition is reported separately with P0B86.

causes.label: Lead P shorted to a lower potential or chassis
Defective input in the battery interface module
Weak cell or NiMH block 16

symptoms: MIL and reduced propulsion power
Auto stop no longer active

P0B89.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit High
P0B89.description: P0B89 covers the opposite case to P0B88: the voltage reported on channel P is above the plausible range. GM's 2012 two-mode hybrids assign P to NiMH block 16 and set the code when the block exceeds 23 V in 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms, Type B, provided no battery controller fault P0A1F is active. In lithium-ion systems GM sets 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in 2 s as the limit, Type A, while the BAS Plus mild hybrid reacts above 4.65 V. GM's 2016 program with a separate sense module allows up to 4.90 V. Overcharging is unlikely to be the cause because the controller stops charging well below these values; a sense lead reaching a higher tap or an input fault is the usual explanation. Expect restricted charging.

causes.label: Lead P in contact with a higher cell tap
Input fault in the cell monitoring electronics
Genuine overvoltage of the cell or block

symptoms: Charging restricted
MIL and hybrid warning

P0B8A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B8A.description: P0B8A is the erratic-signal member of the channel P group. There is no public manufacturer documentation for it: GM describes open, rationality, low and high diagnostics for sense P in its 2016 and 2019 tables, but none for an intermittent signal, and the Ford bulletins stop at channel N. The code exists because CARB 1968.2 requires the voltage sensors of a hybrid battery to be monitored and malfunctions to be stored under distinct codes. If set, the picture would be a channel P value that briefly drops out or spikes, for instance through a fatigued wire near a bend in the sense harness or a connector that loses contact when the pack warms up. Readings in live data may look normal between the events.

causes.label: Fatigued wire at a bend of the sense harness
Connector losing contact as the pack warms up
Sporadic fault in the cell monitoring chip

symptoms: Warning lamp that goes out again
Occasional engine start without demand on hybrids

P0B8B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit
P0B8B.description: P0B8B marks an open circuit on voltage sense Q, the seventeenth channel. In GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid tables Q is the first channel whose open test is blocked by code P1B37 instead of P1B36, which suggests it sits in the next measuring group of the battery interface module; the criterion stays lines N and N-1 below 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. GM's 2019 battery controller uses 0.8 s in a 1.6 s window, the 2016 version 0.6 s, both Type A with the 1.3 V and 36 mV criteria. The 2011 Volt list includes P0B8B as well. The two-mode NiMH trucks have no circuit code for block 17. Ford does not list it. Typically the vehicle restricts or blocks electric operation until repaired.

causes.label: Sense lead Q open between cell tap and module
Loose or corroded connector at the second measuring group
Fault in the battery interface module

symptoms: MIL and service vehicle message
Electric operation blocked or limited
Fuel consumption rises on hybrids

P0B8C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Range/Performance
P0B8C.description: P0B8C is set when channel Q reports a voltage that fails the plausibility test against the other cells or the pack. On GM's 2012 two-mode trucks Q is NiMH block 17; the battery pack control module takes block 17 and block 18, multiplies each by twenty and compares with the measured pack voltage, failing beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B. GM's lithium-ion programs instead check that cell Q follows the average: the 2016 Volt within 7 of 8 seconds, the Cadillac ELR in 20 of 40 samples, the 2019 controllers in 35 of 40 samples with a 0.005 V trend, all Type A. Because the value itself is within limits, the driver may notice little beyond the MIL. A software update or replacement of the monitoring electronics resolves most cases.

causes.label: Monitoring electronics misreading channel Q
Outdated battery controller software
Block 17 or 18 voltage deviating on two-mode NiMH packs

symptoms: MIL with little change in driving
Usable battery capacity reduced

P0B8D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Low
P0B8D.description: P0B8D reports a voltage on sense Q below the lowest credible cell value. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers in the 2016 and 2019 tables use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, and the 2016 program with a separate sense module 0.20 V with 14 of 18 samples. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid applies 1.4 V, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. In the 2012 two-mode NiMH pack Q is block 17 and the battery pack control module requires blocks 17 and 18 both under 2 V for 15 of 20 samples. The low test is suppressed while an open-line fault is active, so P0B8B takes precedence for a broken lead. Shorts in the sense path are the leading cause; a real deep discharge of the cell would normally trigger further battery codes too.

causes.label: Short in the Q sense path to a lower potential
Sense module input reading low
Cell or block 17 deeply discharged

symptoms: MIL and reduced power mode
Engine runs more often on hybrids

P0B8E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit High
P0B8E.description: Channel Q reporting an implausibly high voltage sets P0B8E. On the 2012 GM two-mode hybrids, where Q is NiMH block 17, the limit is 23 V for 15 of 20 samples, Type B, checked only while the 12 V system lies between 9 and 18 V. GM's lithium-ion programs work at cell level: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in 2 s in the 2016 and 2019 battery controllers, more than 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples where a separate battery sense module measures, all Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid limit is 4.65 V. As with the other high codes of this family, wiring and measuring input are far more often to blame than the cell; a damaged harness that lets lead Q touch the next tap is a classic finding. Charging and regeneration are limited.

causes.label: Damaged harness letting lead Q touch the next tap
Measuring input of channel Q reading high
Real cell overvoltage after a balancing failure

symptoms: Regeneration and charging limited
MIL and battery system warning

P0B8F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B8F.description: P0B8F closes the channel Q group and stands for a sense Q signal that is erratic rather than absent or out of range. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's tables for sense Q, from the 2011 Volt to the 2019 battery controllers, list circuit, range, low and high monitors only, and the Ford Fusion bulletin ends four channels earlier at N. CARB 1968.2 forms the basis: it calls for monitoring of the battery voltage sensors in a hybrid energy storage system and for codes that lead a technician to the faulty part. Physically, an erratic Q reading would point to an unstable connection between tap and measuring chip, such as a cracked crimp, a damaged flexible circuit or a cold solder joint. The next channel, R, starts at P0B90.

causes.label: Cracked crimp at the channel Q tap
Damaged flexible circuit between cells and monitoring board
Cold solder joint at the measuring chip

symptoms: Sporadic hybrid or EV warning
Power briefly reduced, normal after restart

P0B90.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit
P0B90.description: P0B90 is stored when the battery controller concludes that the tap of sense R, the eighteenth cell channel, is open or too resistive. GM's 2019 battery energy control module runs seven cases for it: neighbouring cells 1.3 V or more apart, a reading under 36 mV while the balancing gate is on, or splice voltages above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a busbar splice). The fault has to be present for 0.8 s within a 1.6 s window and is Type A. The 2016 Volt and ELR use the same cases with a 0.6 s window. Oddly, GM's first-generation Volt tables of 2011 to 2015 contain no P0B90 at all, although they list the circuit codes of S to V. Range, low and high faults of R are P0B91 to P0B93.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or broken tap of sense lead R
Excessive resistance at a splice or busbar joint feeding channel R
Faulty measuring or balancing input on the cell monitoring board

symptoms: MIL with service hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced propulsion power or no ready mode
Charging interrupted or refused

P0B91.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit Range/Performance
P0B91.description: Here the wiring of sense R is intact, but its value does not behave like a real cell. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain processor demands that cell R moves at least 0.005 V in the same direction whenever the cell average shifts by more than 0.022 V; 35 failures out of 40 samples at 100 ms give a Type A fault. The 2016 Volt allows 7 s of failure in an 8 s window, the ELR 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms. On the 2012 two-mode trucks R is nickel-metal hydride block 18: blocks 18 and 19 are each multiplied by twenty, and if both estimates miss the pack voltage by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, P0B91 is set as Type B. A frozen measuring channel or controller software is the usual suspect.

causes.label: Measuring channel R reporting a stuck value
Outdated battery controller or hybrid processor software
Block 18 or 19 voltage drifting on two-mode NiMH packs

symptoms: MIL on, vehicle often drives normally
Less electric assist or regenerative braking

P0B92.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit Low
P0B92.description: P0B92 stands for an implausibly low reading on sense R. In GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 the limit is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A; the test is suspended while an open sense line fault is active, so a broken lead appears as P0B90 rather than P0B92. Programmes with a separate battery sensor module (GM 16OBDG02) use under 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples. The eAssist mild hybrid applies 1.4 V, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. In the 2012 two-mode trucks R is NiMH block 18, and blocks 18 and 19 must both read under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples (Type B). A short of the sense lead to ground or to a lower cell is the classic cause.

causes.label: Sense lead R chafed through and touching ground or a lower cell
Failed input for channel R on the cell monitoring board
Cell or block on channel R genuinely collapsed

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system message
Propulsion limited, possibly no restart

P0B93.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit High
P0B93.description: A reading on sense R above anything a healthy cell could produce sets P0B93. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 use 4.8 V or more, held 1.4 s within 2 s, as a Type A fault. The 16OBDG02 programme with its own battery sensor module draws the line at 4.90 V, 14 of 18 samples. GM's eAssist mild hybrid already reacts above 4.65 V (7 of 10 samples, Type B). On the 2012 two-mode trucks the channel is nickel-metal hydride block 18, which must exceed 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Because a cell this high would be dangerous, an electrical fault is far more likely: a sense lead touching a higher potential, or a damaged measuring input on the monitoring board.

causes.label: Sense lead R in contact with a higher cell potential
Damaged measuring input for channel R
Cell on channel R actually overcharged

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning
Charging or regeneration cut back
Reduced power mode

P0B94.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense R Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B94.description: No manufacturer documents P0B94 publicly. The code is reserved for a sense R signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing steadily. GM monitors channel R in six table sets between 2011 and 2019, but every one of those tables stops at the circuit, range, low and high monitors; an intermittent test does not appear. The legal basis is CARB 1968.2, which requires the voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system to be monitored like any other input and wants fault codes that point to the smallest replaceable unit. In practice such a fault would come from a connection that opens under vibration or heat, for instance a cracked crimp or a hairline crack in a flexible circuit.

causes.label: Crimp or terminal of lead R opening under vibration
Hairline crack in the flexible circuit carrying channel R
Moisture or contamination in the monitoring board connector

symptoms: Warning appears and disappears between trips
Short power reductions, normal after restart

P0B95.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit
P0B95.description: P0B95 reports that the sense S lead, channel nineteen, no longer connects its cell reliably to the monitoring electronics. GM programmes with a separate battery sensor module (16OBDG02) measure this directly: after each normal reading the balancing gates switch in a test pattern, current flows through the sense wires and the voltage drop is turned into a line resistance. Above 30.00 (the table gives no unit) in 7 of 9 samples at 100 ms, the code sets as Type A. GM's eAssist mild hybrid instead needs lines N and N-1 both under 1.4 V plus a jump of more than 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B, and stays quiet while P1B37 is active. The 2019 lithium-ion controller uses its seven cases with 0.8 s in 1.6 s.

causes.label: High resistance in sense lead S from corrosion or a loose terminal
Sense lead S broken at the cell connector
Defective input of the battery sensor module for channel S

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning
Vehicle may refuse ready mode
Cell balancing no longer effective

P0B96.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit Range/Performance
P0B96.description: P0B96 is a plausibility code: the voltage of sense S looks electrically valid but fails to track the rest of the pack. GM's eAssist mild hybrid requires cell S to move at least half as much as the other cells once the average changes by more than 0.045 V, judged over 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms, Type B. The 16OBDG02 programme accepts a trend of 0.002 V and sets Type A after 35 of 40 evaluations, while the 2019 hybrid processor wants 0.005 V. On the 2012 two-mode trucks S is block 19, and the check scales blocks 19 and 20 by twenty and compares them with the pack voltage, with more than 70 V deviation in 160 of 170 samples leading to Type B. Circuit, low and high faults of S are excluded first.

causes.label: Measuring channel S frozen or lagging behind the other cells
Battery controller calibration requiring a software update
Block 19 or 20 out of step with the pack on two-mode NiMH batteries

symptoms: MIL with little or no change in driving
Electric assist reduced at times

P0B97.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit Low
P0B97.description: With P0B97 the controller sees sense S pulled close to zero. In the 2012 two-mode trucks, where S is the nickel-metal hydride block 19, the battery pack control module only sets it when block 19 and block 20 are both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, with the 12 V system between 9 and 18 V. GM's lithium-ion packs work cell by cell: 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s in 2 s on the 2016 Volt and the 2019 controller, Type A, and under 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples in the 16OBDG02 programme. The eAssist mild hybrid sets it below 1.4 V, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. An open sense line fault takes priority, so P0B97 points more to a short than to a broken lead.

causes.label: Sense lead S shorted to ground or to the next lower cell
Defective channel S input on the monitoring board
Cell or NiMH block on channel S actually discharged

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning message
Restricted power, engine may run more often on hybrids

P0B98.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit High
P0B98.description: P0B98 marks a sense S value that is too high to be a cell voltage. The thresholds vary with the battery chemistry and controller: GM's 2016 Volt and 2019 battery controllers flag 4.8 V or more after 1.4 s in 2 s (Type A), the 16OBDG02 programme 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples (Type A), and the eAssist mild hybrid more than 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples with the 12 V supply above 8.8 V (Type B). On the 2012 two-mode trucks S is NiMH block 19 and its limit is 23 V, 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Like the low test, the high test waits until open sense line faults are ruled out. The fix is usually wiring or the monitoring board; a truly overcharged cell is rare but must be excluded.

causes.label: Sense lead S shorted to a higher cell or busbar
Measuring chip reading channel S incorrectly
Real overvoltage of the cell or block on channel S

symptoms: MIL and service hybrid system message
Charging and regeneration limited

P0B99.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense S Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B99.description: P0B99 is the erratic variant within the sense S group. A public manufacturer description does not exist. GM's tables cover channel S from the 2011 Volt via the 2012 two-mode trucks and eAssist to the 2019 controllers, yet only with circuit, range, low and high codes (P0B95 to P0B98). CARB 1968.2 obliges manufacturers to monitor battery voltage sensors of a hybrid storage system for circuit and rationality faults and to separate the fault codes by replaceable unit, which is why J2012 reserves this slot. Should a vehicle set it, the technician would look for a sense S connection that works most of the time but breaks briefly, typically a fretting terminal or a cracked solder joint on the board.

causes.label: Fretting corrosion on the terminal of sense lead S
Cracked solder joint for channel S on the monitoring board
Harness chafing that only shorts under movement

symptoms: Sporadic hybrid warning without a pattern
Code often stored as history, hard to reproduce

P0B9A.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense T Circuit
P0B9A.description: P0B9A is the open-circuit code for sense T, the twentieth cell channel. GM uses it only on lithium-ion packs. The 2011 Volt compares adjacent cells for a difference above 1 V and checks the busbar cap voltage against 0.7 V; the 2016 Volt and ELR raise the adjacent-cell limit to 1.3 V, add a balancing-gate test below 36 mV and decide within 0.6 s, and the 2019 controller keeps those values but stretches the window to 0.8 s of 1.6 s, Type A in both cases. The 2012 two-mode trucks also have a channel T, their last nickel-metal hydride block 20, yet their tables carry range, low and high codes for it and no circuit code. A genuinely open lead usually means opening the high-voltage pack.

causes.label: Open sense lead T at the cell tab or connector
Poor busbar or splice joint in the channel T path
Monitoring board input for channel T failed

symptoms: MIL, hybrid or EV system warning
Ready mode or charging blocked

P0B9B.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense T Circuit Range/Performance
P0B9B.description: On the 2012 two-mode trucks sense T is block 20, the last of their twenty nickel-metal hydride blocks, and P0B9B shows how GM handles the missing neighbour: block 20 alone is multiplied by twenty and compared with the pack voltage, and a gap above 70 V in 160 of 170 samples sets the code as Type B. All other channels there use a pair of blocks. On lithium-ion packs the code means that cell T does not follow the pack average: the 2019 hybrid processor demands 0.005 V of movement when the average shifts by more than 0.022 V (35 of 40 samples, Type A), the 2016 Volt the same with a 7 s in 8 s window, and eAssist half the average movement in 20 of 40 samples, Type B.

causes.label: Channel T measurement stuck or sluggish
Block 20 voltage diverging from pack voltage on two-mode NiMH packs
Faulty pack voltage reference used for the comparison

symptoms: MIL, drivability usually unchanged
Hybrid assist or EV range slightly reduced

P0B9C.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense T Circuit Low
P0B9C.description: P0B9C signals that sense T reads too low. On the 2012 two-mode trucks this is block 20, and because no block 21 exists the low test there looks at block 20 alone: below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, while channels R and S each need their upper neighbour to read low as well. GM's lithium-ion controllers from the 2016 Volt to 2019 work with 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, the 16OBDG02 programme with under 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples, and the eAssist mild hybrid with 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. Open sense line faults are evaluated first. For the driver the result is a warning and reduced power until the cause is repaired.

causes.label: Sense lead T shorted to ground or a lower potential
Weak or discharged NiMH block 20 on two-mode packs
Failed measuring input for channel T

symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning
Reduced power, engine may not shut off on hybrids

P0B9D.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense T Circuit High
P0B9D.description: If sense T reports more voltage than its cell can hold, the battery controller stores P0B9D. GM documents it on several systems. The 2019 battery energy control module and the 2016 Volt set it at 4.8 V or above for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, and only when no open sense line fault is pending. The 16OBDG02 programme with a dedicated battery sensor module uses 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples. The eAssist mild hybrid sets it above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. In the 2012 two-mode trucks the channel is block 20, the final NiMH block, with a limit of 23 V and 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Most such readings come from wiring touching a higher potential or a faulty measuring input.

causes.label: Sense lead T shorted to a higher cell or busbar
Measuring input for channel T drifting high
Cell or block T genuinely overcharged

symptoms: MIL and service hybrid or EV system message
Charging power reduced

P0B9E.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense T Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0B9E.description: P0B9E would describe a sense T signal that flickers. It lacks any public manufacturer documentation. Even the 2012 two-mode trucks, whose last NiMH block is channel T, monitor it only for range, low and high, and GM's lithium-ion controllers add a circuit test but no intermittent one. The requirement behind the whole code family comes from CARB 1968.2: battery voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system are monitored components, and manufacturers must store separate codes that lead to the smallest part replaceable in service. A technician facing this code would wiggle-test the channel T wiring while watching the cell voltage live and look for a reading that dips or spikes for a fraction of a second.

causes.label: Loose or spread terminal in the channel T connector
Connection that opens with temperature changes
Electrical interference coupling into sense lead T

symptoms: Intermittent warning lamp
Occasional brief loss of electric drive

P0B9F.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit
P0B9F.description: P0B9F covers an open or high-resistance sense U lead, channel twenty-one. From U onward the 2012 two-mode trucks drop out, as their pack has only twenty blocks, so this code is a lithium-ion matter at GM. In the eAssist mild hybrid the test is the familiar one, lines N and N-1 both under 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V within 200 ms in 7 of 10 samples, Type B, but it is now blocked by P1B38 instead of P1B37. The 16OBDG02 programme measures the sense line resistance and sets above 30.00 in 7 of 9 samples, Type A. The 2016 Volt and ELR decide in 0.6 s, the 2019 controller in 0.8 s of 1.6 s, both on adjacent-cell differences of 1.3 V and splice checks.

causes.label: Sense lead U interrupted or detached from its cell
Corroded terminal raising the resistance of lead U
Fault in the balancing circuit used for the channel U test

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
No start or ready mode on some vehicles
Charging not possible

P0BA0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit Range/Performance
P0BA0.description: P0BA0 tells the technician that channel U gives a number, but the number does not move with the pack. GM checks this rationality only on lithium-ion systems, since the two-mode NiMH trucks end at block 20. The Cadillac ELR of 2016 reacts to the smallest movement: when the average cell voltage changes by more than 0.006 V, cell U must follow, and 20 failures in 40 samples at 200 ms set a Type A fault. The Volt of the same year looks at 0.022 V of average movement and a 7 s in 8 s window, the 2019 hybrid processor at 0.005 V with 35 of 40 samples, and eAssist at half the average movement, Type B. Circuit, low and high faults are excluded before the test runs, so wiring is less likely than the controller.

causes.label: Measuring channel U holding a fixed value
Software or calibration issue in the battery controller
Cell U behaving differently from its neighbours due to ageing

symptoms: MIL, often without driver-noticeable change
Electric range may be reduced

P0BA1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit Low
P0BA1.description: P0BA1 is stored when sense U reads close to zero. GM's lithium-ion controllers of the 2016 Volt and ELR and of 2019 treat 0.2 V or less over 1.4 s in a 2 s window as a Type A fault, provided no open sense line, lost slave communication or balancing fault is already active. The 16OBDG02 programme with its own battery sensor module uses under 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples. GM's eAssist mild hybrid applies a much higher limit of 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. The two-mode NiMH trucks have no channel U. A short in the sense lead or a failed measuring input is the most likely finding.

causes.label: Sense lead U shorted towards ground or a lower cell
Dead measuring input for channel U
Cell U internally shorted or deeply discharged

symptoms: MIL and EV or hybrid system warning
Propulsion power limited

P0BA2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit High
P0BA2.description: P0BA2 flags an excessive voltage on channel U. GM's eAssist mild hybrid uses the lowest threshold of the documented systems: above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples with the 12 V supply above 8.8 V, Type B. The 2016 Volt and the 2019 battery controller set it at 4.8 V or more held for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A; the 16OBDG02 programme at above 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples, Type A. As with the low code, the high test is held back while an open sense line or module communication fault is active. Channel U does not exist on the twenty-block two-mode trucks. Before replacing parts, the actual cell voltage should be measured, because a lead touching a higher potential is far more common than a real overcharge.

causes.label: Sense lead U in contact with a higher potential
Measuring IC misreading channel U
Cell U actually overcharged

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning
Charging stopped early

P0BA3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense U Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BA3.description: Within the sense U group, P0BA3 is the slot for a signal that is present but unsteady. No manufacturer documents it publicly; GM, the only maker whose tables cover channel U in detail, uses P0B9F to P0BA2 and nothing more. CARB 1968.2 demands monitoring of the hybrid storage system's voltage sensors and separate codes per repairable unit, and SAE reserves the intermittent code so that a manufacturer could report unstable sensing separately from a hard open or short. Physically this points to a connection that breaks for milliseconds, such as a fatigued crimp, a loose screw at a busbar tap or vibration damage to a flexible printed circuit. Repair follows the same path as for the circuit code.

causes.label: Fatigued crimp on sense lead U
Loose fastener at the busbar tap of channel U
Vibration damage to the flexible printed circuit

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief reduced-power events

P0BA4.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit
P0BA4.description: P0BA4 reports an open or poorly connected sense V lead, the twenty-second channel and the last before W begins at P0BA9. GM's 2019 battery energy control module recognises it through seven cases, including 1.3 V between neighbouring cells, less than 36 mV with the balancing gate on and splice voltages above 0.1 or 0.5 V, with 0.8 s of failure in 1.6 s, Type A. The 2011 Volt already listed P0BA4 among its open sense line codes. In GM's 16OBDG02 programme a measured line resistance above 30.00 in 7 of 9 samples triggers it, in the eAssist mild hybrid low readings on lines N and N-1 together with a 0.5 V jump, Type B, gated by P1B38. Without a good sense lead the pack cannot balance or protect that cell.

causes.label: Broken or unplugged sense lead V
High-resistance splice or busbar joint on channel V
Cell monitoring board fault on channel V

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning
Vehicle may not become ready to drive
Charging blocked

P0BA5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit Range/Performance
P0BA5.description: P0BA5 describes a sense V value that stays within limits but fails a rationality check against the other cells. GM's 16OBDG02 programme demands a trend of at least 0.002 V in the same direction as the average whenever that average moves more than 0.022 V, with 35 failures in 40 evaluations giving Type A. The 2019 hybrid processor works the same way with 0.005 V. For the 2016 model year GM lists two variants: the Volt with a 7 s in 8 s window and the ELR with 0.006 V of average movement and 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms. GM's eAssist expects half the average movement, Type B. Since the test is skipped while circuit, low or high faults are active, P0BA5 alone points to the measurement rather than an open lead.

causes.label: Channel V reading stuck while other cells move
Battery controller firmware needing reprogramming
Aged cell V responding differently to load

symptoms: MIL, little change in driving
Reduced regeneration or assist possible

P0BA6.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit Low
P0BA6.description: A sense V reading that collapses towards zero produces P0BA6. The threshold depends on the system: GM's eAssist mild hybrid uses under 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples with at least 8.8 V on the 12 V side, Type B, while GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 go down to 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A. The 16OBDG02 programme sets it below 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples. Because these tests are blocked by an active open sense line fault, P0BA4 would be reported first if the lead were simply broken; P0BA6 alone tends to mean a short to a lower potential or a failed input. The driver sees a hybrid or EV warning and reduced power.

causes.label: Sense lead V shorted to ground or a lower cell
Monitoring board input for channel V failed
Cell V genuinely collapsed

symptoms: MIL and service hybrid or EV system message
Power limited, restart may be refused

P0BA7.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit High
P0BA7.description: P0BA7 is the high-voltage plausibility code for channel V. The battery controller compares the measured value against a ceiling no healthy cell should reach: 4.8 V for 1.4 s within 2 s in GM's 2016 Volt and ELR and in the 2019 battery energy control module (Type A), 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples of 100 ms in the 16OBDG02 programme (Type A), and 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples in the eAssist mild hybrid (Type B). Each of these checks waits for the open sense line monitor to pass. A high reading usually comes from a sense lead V pressed against a higher cell tab or busbar, or from a measuring chip that has lost its reference, and only rarely from a cell actually overcharged.

causes.label: Sense lead V touching a higher cell tab or busbar
Measuring chip with faulty reference reading channel V high
Cell V really overcharged

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning
Charging and regeneration reduced

P0BA8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense V Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BA8.description: P0BA8 completes the five codes of channel V and is meant for an unstable rather than a failed sense V signal. There is no public manufacturer documentation for it. GM covers channel V in its 2011 Volt, eAssist, 2016 and 2019 tables but never with an intermittent monitor, only with P0BA4 to P0BA7. The code exists because CARB 1968.2 requires battery voltage sensors of hybrid storage systems to be monitored and fault codes to isolate the smallest replaceable unit, and J2012 provides an intermittent slot for every sense channel. A fault of this kind would typically be traced to a connection that loses contact under vibration or thermal cycling. Channel W follows from P0BA9.

causes.label: Contact of lead V lost intermittently under vibration
Joint on channel V opening with thermal cycling
Corroded connector pin for channel V

symptoms: Occasional hybrid or EV warning
Fault not reproducible during short workshop test

P0BA9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit
P0BA9.description: P0BA9 opens the W group, the twenty-third cell voltage channel, and flags a sense lead that is open or badly connected. GM's 2019 battery energy control module checks seven cases, ranging from a reading under 36 mV while the balancing gate of that cell is switched on to at least 1.3 V between neighbouring cells and splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V at busbar joints; 0.8 s of failure within 1.6 s sets it as Type A. The 2016 Volt module uses a 0.6 s window instead. GM's eAssist mild hybrid needs readings under 1.4 V on lines N and N-1 plus a change of more than 0.5 V within 200 ms in seven of ten samples, Type B. With the lead lost, the cell behind it can neither be balanced nor protected.

causes.label: Broken, chafed or unplugged sense lead W
High-resistance busbar or splice joint at channel W
Failed input on the cell monitoring board for W

symptoms: MIL with hybrid or EV system warning
Reduced propulsion power or no ready mode
Charging interrupted or refused

P0BAA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit Range/Performance
P0BAA.description: Here the W reading is not missing but implausible: it fails to follow the rest of the pack. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain control processor 2 watches for the average cell voltage to move more than 0.022 V between samples and then expects channel W to trend at least 0.005 V in the same direction; 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms give a Type A fault. The 16OBDG02 programme applies the same logic with 0.002 V. The eAssist system is more tolerant and only asks the cell to move half as far as the others once the average shifts more than 0.045 V, 20 of 40 samples, Type B. In the 2011 Volt tables W appears as sensor 23 of the rationality check. Drivers often notice nothing beyond the warning lamp.

causes.label: Measuring input for W frozen at a fixed value
Battery controller software needing an update
Cell W reacting differently to load because of ageing

symptoms: Warning lamp with little change in driving
Possibly limited regeneration or electric assist

P0BAB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit Low
P0BAB.description: A W channel reading at or near zero sets P0BAB. How low is too low depends on the battery: GM's lithium-ion modules of 2016 and 2019 react to 0.2 V or less held for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, and the 16OBDG02 programme to under 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples at 100 ms. The eAssist mild hybrid already fails below 1.4 V, seven of ten samples, as long as the 12 V supply exceeds 8.8 V and P1B38 is not active; that fault is Type B. All of these tests stand down while an open sense line fault is present, so a simply broken lead shows up as P0BA9. P0BAB on its own suggests a short towards a lower potential, a dead measuring input or a deeply discharged cell. Power and charging are usually restricted.

causes.label: Sense lead W shorted to a lower cell potential
Measuring input for W on the monitoring board failed
Cell W deeply discharged or internally shorted

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning and MIL
Reduced power output
Charging limited or blocked

P0BAC.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit High
P0BAC.description: P0BAC is the upper counterpart to P0BAB: channel W reports more voltage than a single cell can plausibly hold. GM sets the limit at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s in the 2011 and 2016 Volt battery modules, which makes it a one-trip fault. The 16OBDG02 programme fails at above 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples, Type A, while the eAssist battery is stricter with more than 4.65 V in seven of ten samples, Type B. A high reading usually comes from a lead touching the potential of the next cell up or from a faulty input, less often from a genuinely overcharged cell. Because overcharging is a safety risk, the controller typically cuts charging and regeneration until the cause is found.

causes.label: Sense lead W in contact with a higher cell potential
Monitoring board input for W reading too high
Cell W actually overcharged after a balancing fault

symptoms: MIL and battery system warning
Charging and regeneration stopped
Possible reduced power mode

P0BAD.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense W Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BAD.description: P0BAD is reserved for a W signal that drops out or jumps for short moments instead of failing outright. No manufacturer documents the code publicly. GM monitors channel W in several programmes, from the 2011 Volt to the eAssist and the 2019 tables, but only through P0BA9 to P0BAC; none of them contains an intermittent test. The slot exists because J2012 gives every sense channel five codes and CARB 1968.2 requires the battery voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system to be monitored with fault codes that point to the smallest replaceable part. If a vehicle did store it, the usual suspects would be a crimp or connector that loses contact under vibration or with temperature changes.

causes.label: Loose or fretting connector pin on lead W
Crimp on lead W opening with temperature changes
Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board input W

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Occasional short power reduction

P0BAE.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense X Circuit
P0BAE.description: Channel X, number twenty-four, starts with P0BAE, the open-lead code. The first-generation Volt of 2011 already detected it through several cases: two neighbouring readings more than 1 V apart, a busbar sense voltage above 0.7 V combined with an implausible cell voltage, or adjacent cells differing by more than 0.5 V on a shared supply line. GM's later 16OBDG02 programme measures the sense line resistance directly and fails it above 30.00 in seven of nine samples, Type A; the unit is not printed. In the 2019 battery energy control module the familiar 1.3 V and 36 mV criteria apply with 0.8 s in 1.6 s. Whichever method is used, the controller loses sight of one cell and normally restricts the battery.

causes.label: Sense lead X broken or disconnected
Loose busbar fastener at the X sensing point
Sense harness X damaged during earlier battery work

symptoms: MIL and service message for the high-voltage system
Vehicle may stay out of ready mode
Charging stops early

P0BAF.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense X Circuit Range/Performance
P0BAF.description: P0BAF covers a sense X signal that is electrically present yet does not behave like a real cell. For model year 2016 GM documents two versions in the same booklet. The Volt controller fails it when X moves in a different direction from the pack average, or by less than 0.005 V while that average moves more than 0.022 V, for 7 s within 8 s, Type A. The ELR variant samples every 200 ms, needs average movement above 0.006 V and fails after 20 of 40 samples, one trip. The eAssist hybrid asks for at least half of the average change, Type B over two trips, and GM's 2019 processor uses a 0.005 V trend test. Since the check pauses during circuit, low or high faults, P0BAF points to a stuck measurement rather than a broken wire.

causes.label: Sense X value stuck while the pack voltage changes
Calibration of the battery controller requiring reprogramming
Cell X with deviating internal resistance
