symptoms: MIL without obvious driving change
Reduced electric range in some cases

P0BB0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense X Circuit Low
P0BB0.description: When channel X reads too low, P0BB0 is stored. In GM's eAssist mild hybrid the battery interface module sets it below 1.4 V in seven of ten samples at 200 ms, provided the 12 V system is above 8.8 V and the group fault P1B38 is not active, as a two-trip Type B fault. The 2011 Volt and the 16OBDG02 programme work with a far lower limit of about 0.2 V, the latter in 14 of 18 samples at 100 ms, Type A. That difference reflects the cell chemistry and how much voltage a healthy cell can lose. Because an open lead is caught first by P0BAE, a stand-alone P0BB0 is more often a short in the sense harness, a failed input or a cell that has collapsed. Expect reduced power and blocked charging.

causes.label: Short between sense lead X and a lower potential
Defective measuring channel X in the monitoring electronics
Cell X collapsed or internally shorted

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL
Electric assist or propulsion reduced
Charging not possible

P0BB1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense X Circuit High
P0BB1.description: P0BB1 means the battery controller sees too much voltage on sense X. In GM's 2019 battery energy control module the threshold is 4.8 V or more, held for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, and the code is Type A, so the MIL comes on in the first trip. The 16OBDG02 programme allows up to 4.90 V and needs 14 failing samples out of 18, while the eAssist battery treats anything above 4.65 V in seven of ten samples as a Type B fault. These tests are suppressed while an open sense line or a lost communication with the cell monitoring slave is active. A real cell at that voltage would be dangerously overcharged, so a wiring fault towards the neighbour cell or a defective input is the more frequent finding.

causes.label: Sense lead X shorted to the next higher cell
Measuring input X drifting high
Cell X genuinely over voltage

symptoms: MIL in the first trip
Charging and regenerative braking disabled

P0BB2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense X Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BB2.description: Of the five X codes, P0BB2 is the only one without any public manufacturer description. It is intended for a sense X signal that flickers, drops out briefly or jumps between values. GM's Volt tables of 2011 and 2016 list channel X with circuit, range, low and high monitors, P0BAE to P0BB1, and no intermittent check. The code therefore rests on the J2012 structure and on CARB 1968.2, which requires hybrid battery voltage sensors to be monitored and the fault to be isolated to the smallest replaceable unit. In practice a technician would look for a contact that opens under vibration, moisture in a connector or a harness rubbing against the module housing.

causes.label: Contact on lead X opening under vibration
Moisture or corrosion in the X sense connector
Harness X chafing against the module housing

symptoms: Intermittent warning lamp
Sporadic hybrid system message

P0BB3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit
P0BB3.description: P0BB3 reports that the sense lead of channel Y, the twenty-fifth cell group, is no longer properly connected. GM's 16OBDG02 programme does not wait for odd voltages but calculates the resistance of the sense line and fails it above 30.00 in seven of nine samples, which is a one-trip Type A fault; the unit is missing in the table. The 2019 battery energy control module instead looks at the cell voltages themselves, for example 1.3 V between neighbours or a reading below 36 mV while that cell is being balanced, with 0.8 s of failure in 1.6 s. The eAssist mild hybrid sets it as a Type B fault when lines N and N-1 both read under 1.4 V and jump by more than 0.5 V. Low and high monitors for Y are blocked while P0BB3 is active.

causes.label: Open circuit in sense lead Y
Corroded or loose terminal raising line resistance at Y
Cell monitoring slave board fault on input Y

symptoms: MIL and high-voltage system warning
Vehicle may not start in electric mode
Charging aborted

P0BB4.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit Range/Performance
P0BB4.description: P0BB4 is a plausibility code: the controller compares how the Y reading changes over time with the behaviour of all other cells. In the 16OBDG02 programme a sample counts as failed when the pack average moves by more than 0.022 V but Y has not trended at least 0.002 V the same way; 35 such results in 40 evaluations set a one-trip Type A fault. The 2019 hybrid powertrain control processor 2 uses the same frame with a 0.005 V trend. For the 2016 Volt the window is 7 s in 8 s. A frozen analogue input or a software problem in the battery controller are the typical findings, while a real cell defect is rarer. Unlike P0BB3, the signal is present, so the car usually keeps driving.

causes.label: Analogue input Y frozen at one value
Battery controller software fault
Weak cell Y with sluggish voltage response

symptoms: MIL, vehicle still drivable
Battery power occasionally limited

P0BB5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit Low
P0BB5.description: P0BB5 stands for a sense Y voltage below the plausible minimum. GM's 2016 Volt module and the 2019 battery energy control module both use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window and flag it as Type A. Before testing, the 2019 module makes sure that no open sense line, no lost communication with the cell monitoring slave and no balancing or internal slave fault is active, and that the second protection self test is not running. The eAssist mild hybrid sets the code below 1.4 V in seven of ten samples, Type B. The likely culprits are a pinched sense wire touching a lower potential, a failed measuring channel or a cell that has really lost its charge. The driver sees a warning and reduced performance.

causes.label: Pinched sense wire Y shorting to a lower potential
Failed measuring channel Y
Cell Y severely discharged

symptoms: Hybrid or EV warning with MIL
Noticeably reduced power

P0BB6.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit High
P0BB6.description: The battery controller logs P0BB6 when the Y channel climbs above a level no healthy cell reaches. GM's first Volt of 2011 put that limit at 4.8 V or more, 1.4 s within 2 s, with the MIL after one trip. The 16OBDG02 programme samples every 100 ms and fails above 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples, Type A; the eAssist battery fails above 4.65 V in seven of ten samples at 200 ms, Type B. A wiring fault that connects the Y input to the potential of the next cell is the most common explanation, followed by a failed input. Overcharging of a single cell is possible after a balancing problem and must be ruled out before the pack is charged again.

causes.label: Sense input Y bridged to the next cell potential
Defective input Y on the monitoring board
Overcharged cell Y after a balancing problem

symptoms: MIL and charging stopped
Regeneration disabled

P0BB7.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Y Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BB7.description: P0BB7 would describe an unstable sense Y signal, one that is mostly correct but drops out or jumps from time to time. No manufacturer publishes a monitor for it. Where GM covers channel Y, in the 16OBDG02 programme and the 2019 battery and hybrid processor tables, it does so with P0BB3 to P0BB6: line resistance, trend comparison, low and high limits. A brief interruption would there show up as a counted failure inside one of those tests rather than under its own code. P0BB7 thus exists as a J2012 placeholder that satisfies the CARB 1968.2 demand for monitored battery voltage sensors. Diagnosis would focus on connectors, crimps and solder joints that react to movement or heat.

causes.label: Intermittent contact in the Y sense connector
Crimp or weld on lead Y opening when hot
Hairline crack in a solder joint of input Y

symptoms: Warning lamp appears now and then
Short-lived power limitation

P0BB8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit
P0BB8.description: P0BB8 is the open-circuit code of channel Z, the twenty-sixth and last cell channel with a generic P0 code. GM packs with more channels continue with manufacturer codes, for example P1B28 for the circuit of AA in the 2019 tables. The 2019 battery energy control module sets P0BB8 through the same seven cases as its neighbours, with 1.3 V between adjacent cells, under 36 mV on an active balancing gate or excessive splice voltage, 0.8 s in 1.6 s, Type A. GM's eAssist uses the voltage of lines N and N-1 below 1.4 V together with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, seven of ten samples, Type B and gated by P1B38. The 2011 Volt already listed P0BB8 among its open sense line faults.

causes.label: Sense lead Z interrupted
Excessive resistance at the splice or busbar of Z
Monitoring electronics input Z defective

symptoms: MIL and stop or service warning for the drive system
Ready mode may be refused
No charging

P0BB9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit Range/Performance
P0BB9.description: With P0BB9 the controller says that sense Z does not track the pack: the value is within limits, but it stays still or moves the wrong way while the other cells change. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain control processor 2 enables the comparison once the system voltage is above 10.20 V and the average cell voltage shifts by more than 0.022 V, then demands a trend of at least 0.005 V on Z; 35 failures in 40 samples are Type A. The 2016 Volt variant fails after 7 s within 8 s. In the eAssist mild hybrid, Z has to follow at least half of an average movement above 0.045 V, 20 of 40 samples, Type B. A recalibrated controller or a replaced monitoring board is a more common fix than a new cell.

causes.label: Z reading static despite changing pack voltage
Monitoring board or controller calibration fault
Cell Z with abnormal charge and discharge behaviour

symptoms: MIL, driving largely unaffected
Possibly lower assist or regeneration

P0BBA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit Low
P0BBA.description: P0BBA is stored when the voltage measured on channel Z falls below the lower limit. In the 16OBDG02 programme the hybrid processor checks Z every 100 ms and fails it below 0.20 V in 14 of 18 samples, a Type A fault, but only with a system voltage above 10.20 V and no open-circuit fault on the cell. GM's 2019 battery energy control module and the 2011 Volt use 0.2 V or less over 1.4 s within 2 s. This rules out a simple open lead, which would have set P0BB8 first. What remains is a short in the Z wiring or connector, a failed channel on the monitoring board or a cell whose voltage has actually collapsed. The battery is normally limited to protect the other cells.

causes.label: Short in the Z sense wiring or connector
Failed channel Z on the monitoring board
Voltage collapse of cell Z

symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV warning
Limited power and charging

P0BBB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit High
P0BBB.description: If the Z channel shows a cell voltage above the upper limit, the controller sets P0BBB. The 2016 Volt battery module uses 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, and checks first that the cell monitoring slave is communicating and no open sense line is reported. The 16OBDG02 programme fails above 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples, and the eAssist mild hybrid fails above 4.65 V in seven of ten samples with a healthy 12 V supply, Type B over two trips. Lithium-ion cells are not meant to exceed these values, so the reading normally points to a short towards the higher neighbour, a faulty input or a corrupted measurement, and only rarely to a truly overcharged cell. Charging is stopped as a precaution.

causes.label: Sense lead Z shorted towards the higher neighbour cell
Faulty measuring input Z
Cell Z overcharged

symptoms: MIL and charging stopped
Reduced regeneration

P0BBC.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Z Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BBC.description: P0BBC closes the generic block of 26 cell voltage channels from A to Z; after it J2012 moves on to pack-level codes such as P0BBD and P0BBE. The code is meant for a Z signal that is unstable rather than absent. There is no manufacturer documentation for it: GM monitors channel Z from the 2011 Volt to the 2019 battery energy control module, but always with P0BB8 to P0BBB only, and no table contains an intermittent monitor. Its basis is CARB 1968.2, which requires battery voltage sensors of hybrid storage systems to be checked and faults to be narrowed down to the smallest replaceable unit. Should it appear, contacts that fail under vibration or heat cycling are the logical starting point.

causes.label: Intermittent contact on sense lead Z
Joint at channel Z opening with heat cycling
Corrosion in the Z sense connector

symptoms: Warning lamp appearing irregularly
Occasional brief loss of electric drive power

P0BBD.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Variation Exceeded Limit
P0BBD.description: P0BBD means the spread between cells or blocks of the pack has grown beyond what the controller accepts. GM used it on the two-mode hybrids, where a difference of more than 1.5 V between adjacent block voltages in three of three samples at 1 s, with battery current above 0.2 A, set a Type B fault labelled as end-of-life deviation. On the Chevrolet Bolt EV, bulletin 22-NA-151 links it to reduced propulsion and charging capped at 30 % and names cases induced by driving style that need reprogramming, otherwise a pack replacement. Volkswagen reports it on the ID.4 from cells with increased self-discharge, Audi on the Q4 e-tron with a drive system that cannot be activated, and Stellantis on the Wrangler 4xe.

causes.label: Cells or modules with increased self-discharge or capacity loss
Controller software or cell capacity adaptation needing an update
Aged battery pack at end of life
Cell balancing unable to equalise the pack

symptoms: MIL or electrical system warning
Reduced propulsion power and capped state of charge
Reduced electric range
Drive system cannot be activated in severe cases

P0BBE.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Voltage Variation
P0BBE.description: P0BBE watches the gap between the highest and the lowest cell voltage in the pack. GM's first-generation Volt sets it when that difference exceeds 0.3 V in 50 of 245 samples taken every 100 ms, provided the cell voltage rationality fault is not active; it is a one-trip Type A fault. Stellantis lists the code on the Jeep Grand Cherokee 4xe and Wrangler 4xe together with P0B24, P0DAB and a state-of-health code, where updated battery pack control module software is the remedy and an unresolved case can end in a no-start. Chrysler's warranty extension for the 2017 to 2021 Pacifica Hybrid replaces the whole high-voltage pack for this code. Its companion P0BBD reports a spread that has exceeded a set limit.

causes.label: Cells drifted apart beyond what balancing can correct
Battery pack control module software needing an update
Defective or aged high-voltage battery pack
Faulty cell voltage measurement simulating a spread

symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning
Reduced electric range or propulsion
Vehicle may not start

P0BBF.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
P0BBF.description: Air-cooled hybrid packs draw cooling air through a 12 V blower that is fed through a fuse and often a relay; the controller watches the voltage reaching the fan, and Toyota even uses that measured supply voltage to correct the fan duty. P0BBF means this feed is open or missing while the fan should be powered. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's Two-Mode hybrid monitors the same feed but reports only the high case, a welded relay, as P0BC1. CARB requires the electrical inputs and outputs of battery thermal management to be monitored. Low and high faults are P0BC0 and P0BC1, faults in the fan's own control line P0A81 to P0A85. Without power the fan stops, the pack warms up and the controller limits power.

causes.label: Blown fuse in the battery fan feed
Fan relay contacts not closing or relay coil open
Open supply wire or loose terminal at the fan connector

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or MIL on
Battery fan silent when it should run
Reduced electric assist in hot weather or under load

P0BC0.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P0BC0.description: P0BC0 reports that the voltage feeding the battery cooling fan is lower than expected while the fan is switched on. A short to ground downstream of the fuse, a corroded connector or a relay with burnt contacts drops the voltage, so the fan turns slowly or not at all. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Toyota's hybrid controller measures the fan supply on the auxiliary battery side and raises the duty when it is low, which shows why a sagging feed matters for cooling. CARB asks for circuit monitoring of all battery thermal management parts. The open case is P0BBF, the high case P0BC1 (GM: welded relay). A weak 12 V battery can cause a sag too, so check it first. Expect reduced power when the pack heats up.

causes.label: Fan supply wire chafed and shorted to ground
Burnt fan relay contacts or corroded terminals causing voltage drop
Weak 12 V auxiliary battery or poor ground
Seizing fan motor pulling excessive current

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or MIL on
Battery fan runs slowly or noticeably weaker
Reduced electric assist when the pack is warm

P0BC1.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan Supply Voltage Circuit High
P0BC1.description: P0BC1 flags voltage on the battery fan feed when there should be none, or more than expected. GM documents it for the battery pack control module of its Two-Mode hybrid SUVs and pickups (Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado, Sierra; 2012 and 2013 tables) as a welded fan relay: with the fan commanded off, a fan monitor voltage of at least 0.9 V in 10 of 20 samples at 100 ms sets it, provided the 12 V system is between 9 and 18 V and no fan circuit code (P0A81) is active. It is Type B, MIL after two trips. A stuck relay keeps the fan running with the vehicle off and drains the 12 V battery. The open and low cases are P0BBF and P0BC0; a fan that keeps turning without this fault is P0A83.

causes.label: Fan relay contacts welded closed
Fan feed shorted to a constant battery voltage wire
Relay control output in the module stuck on

symptoms: MIL on after two trips
Battery fan keeps running after the vehicle is switched off
Discharged 12 V battery after standing

P0BC2.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E Circuit
P0BC2.description: Battery temperature sensor E is the fifth thermistor in the high-voltage pack; GM's Chevrolet Volt bulletin 18-NA-342 lists the E codes as temperature sensor 5 of nine. P0BC2 is the general circuit code, used when the controller detects an electrical fault without classing it as low, high or erratic. GM's hybrid tables report only the specific siblings P0BC3 to P0BC6. NHTSA's summary of an Audi pending service solution for 2027 Q6 and A6 e-tron models names P0BC2 with a failure type byte among implausible temperature sensor errors. CARB requires battery temperature sensors to be monitored for circuit faults. With one value missing the controller limits charge and discharge power. The sensor sits inside the pack, so checks call for high-voltage safety procedures.

causes.label: Loose or corroded connector of sensor E at the sensing board
Failed thermistor E
Faulty input on the battery sensing board or module

symptoms: Hybrid or EV system warning and MIL
Reduced power or charging rate
Battery cooling running more than usual

P0BC3.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E Circuit Range/Performance
P0BC3.description: P0BC3 is the plausibility check for battery temperature sensor E, GM's sensor 5: its reading is compared with the other pack sensors, which should agree closely. GM's 2016 hybrid table fails it when E is more than 25 °C away from the average of the others in 50 of 67 samples; the 2018 CT6 plug-in table more than 20 °C for 5 s within 6.7 s; the eAssist mild hybrid (13OBDG05C) allows only 8.55 °C, and only after the module has been off for more than six hours. All are Type B, two trips. The check is suspended while circuit codes are active, so it points to a sensor that reads wrongly but in range, or to a real hot spot. Volt bulletin 18-NA-342 counts it among codes that set falsely in cold weather and fixes them by reprogramming.

causes.label: Sensor E drifting or poorly seated on its cell group
Module software setting the code falsely in the cold (GM Volt)
Real local hot spot from a weak cell group or blocked airflow

symptoms: MIL on after two trips
Battery too cold or reduced power message
Limited charge and discharge power

P0BC4.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E Circuit Low
P0BC4.description: Sensor E is an NTC thermistor with a pull-up resistor, so its voltage falls as it gets hotter; a short to ground therefore looks like an extremely hot cell group. GM's 2016 table sets P0BC4 when the converted value exceeds 160 °C in 8 of 10 samples; the 2011 Volt table and GM's 2019 battery module table use above 87.5 °C for 1.4 s within 2 s; the eAssist mild hybrid flags a sense voltage under 0.3 V, about 90 °C, in 7 of 10 samples. All are Type B, two trips. Volt bulletin 18-NA-342 names it sensor 5 circuit low voltage. Its counterpart is P0BC5 (open circuit, reads very cold); a genuinely overheated pack is reported as P0A7E. Because the controller must assume heat, it cuts charge and discharge power and may run cooling at full speed.

causes.label: Sensor E signal wire shorted to ground inside the pack
Internally shorted thermistor E
Moisture or contamination on the sensing board

symptoms: MIL on after two trips
Implausibly high temperature for sensor E on the scan tool
Reduced power and battery fan or cooling at full speed

P0BC5.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E Circuit High
P0BC5.description: P0BC5 reports that battery temperature sensor E delivers a voltage above its valid range. With GM's NTC sensors that reads as extreme cold, pointing to an open wire, a backed-out pin at the sensing board or a cracked thermistor. GM's 2016 table sets it below -69 °C in 8 of 10 samples, the 2011 Volt table and GM's 2019 battery module table below -40 °C for 1.4 s within 2 s, and the eAssist mild hybrid above 4.63 V, about -45 °C, in 7 of 10 samples; all Type B, two trips. On the Chevrolet Volt, bulletin 18-NA-342 links these codes to a Battery Too Cold message at ambient temperatures above -25 °C and prescribes reprogramming. Its counterpart is P0BC4. A pack the controller believes frozen gets strict charge and power limits.

causes.label: Open sensor E wire or backed-out pin at the sensing board
Cracked or open thermistor E
Module software misreading in the cold (GM Volt, reprogramming)

symptoms: MIL on after two trips
Battery too cold, plug in to warm message
Very limited power or charging

P0BC6.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Temperature Sensor E Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BC6.description: P0BC6 flags erratic behaviour of battery temperature sensor E: the reading jumps far faster than the heavy battery mass could warm or cool. GM documents the method in its 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables (16OBDG02, 18OBDG02). Sampling every 100 ms, the controller adds up the absolute changes of the sensor value over a 10-sample window; a sum above 10 fails the window, and 4 failed windows out of 5 store the code as Type B, two trips, provided system voltage is above 10.2 V. The same logic covers the other pack sensors. The older Volt, Two-Mode and eAssist tables list no erratic code for sensor E. Typical culprits are a loose terminal, a cracked wire or a connector not fully latched after pack work; if several sensors jump at once, suspect the sensing board.

causes.label: Loose terminal or unlatched connector of sensor E
Cracked or chafed sensor wire breaking contact intermittently
Sensing board fault affecting several temperature inputs

symptoms: MIL on after two trips
Sensor E value jumping on the scan tool
Occasional power reduction

P0BC7.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Sense Circuit/Open
P0BC7.description: Many battery cooling fans report their actual speed back to the controller as a pulse signal; Toyota patents describe a rotation sensor on the fan motor whose measured speed is compared with the target. P0BC7 means this feedback line for fan 1 is open or carries no usable signal. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables cover the same feedback only through P0BC8, P0BC9 and P0BCA. CARB requires the electrical inputs of battery thermal management to be monitored. The fan may still turn, but the controller can no longer confirm it and usually limits power to protect the pack. Faults in the drive circuit are P0A81 to P0A85; fan 2 feedback has its own codes P0D5F to P0D63.

causes.label: Open feedback wire or loose pin at the fan connector
Failed speed sensor or electronics inside the fan unit
Faulty feedback input in the controlling module

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or MIL on
Reduced electric assist or charging power
Fan audible even though the code reports no feedback

P0BC8.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Sense Range/Performance
P0BC8.description: P0BC8 compares the speed fed back by battery cooling fan 1 with what the controller commanded. GM's 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables run two checks. With the fan enabled at 11 to 89 % duty for more than 11 s, the filtered difference between commanded and reported speed must stay inside calibrated limits; large errors fail within seconds, small ones after up to 43 s. With the fan off for more than 20 s, a reported speed above 120 rpm fails in 24 of 32 samples at 250 ms. It is Type B, two trips, and waits while drive or sense circuit codes are active. A dusty or worn fan that cannot reach its speed is the usual cause; a fan turning while commanded off points to a stuck drive. The circuit cases are P0BC7, P0BC9 and P0BCA.

causes.label: Dust-clogged impeller, blocked intake or worn fan bearing
Fan keeps running while commanded off (stuck drive or relay)
Fan electronics reporting a wrong speed

symptoms: MIL on after two trips
Weak airflow or unusual fan noise from the battery intake
Reduced electric assist when the pack warms up

P0BC9.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Sense Circuit Low
P0BC9.description: P0BC9 means the speed feedback of battery cooling fan 1 is implausibly low while the fan is running. GM evaluates the feedback as a frequency: in its 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables the code counts a failure when the frequency stays below 8 Hz with the fan enabled at 11 to 89 % duty for more than 8 s and system voltage above 10.2 V; 16 failures in 20 samples at 250 ms set it as Type B, two trips. A frequency near zero comes either from a fan that is not turning or from a feedback line shorted to ground or interrupted. The high case is P0BCA, a speed that is merely too far from the target is P0BC8, and drive circuit faults are P0A81 to P0A85. Expect power limits when the pack warms up.

causes.label: Fan seized, blocked or without power
Feedback wire shorted to ground or interrupted
Failed speed sensor inside the fan unit

symptoms: MIL on after two trips
No airflow from the battery cooling fan
Reduced power when the battery gets warm

P0BCA.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Sense Circuit High
P0BCA.description: P0BCA means the speed feedback of battery cooling fan 1 is implausibly high. GM's 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables count a failure when the feedback frequency exceeds 290 Hz with the fan enabled at 11 to 89 % duty for more than 8 s and system voltage above 10.2 V; 16 failures in 20 samples at 250 ms set it as Type B, two trips. No real fan reaches that frequency, so the cause is electrical: noise coupled into the feedback line, a line shorted to another signal or to voltage, or fan electronics sending garbage. Check wire routing and grounds before replacing the fan. The low case is P0BC9, speed errors within range P0BC8, an open line P0BC7. While the feedback is untrusted the controller may limit power.

causes.label: Electrical noise on the feedback line from poor routing or a bad ground
Feedback wire shorted to voltage or another signal
Fan electronics sending an invalid speed signal

symptoms: MIL on after two trips
Implausible fan speed reading on the scan tool
Possible power reduction

P0BCB.title: Hybrid/EV Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Sense Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BCB.description: P0BCB flags a speed feedback from battery cooling fan 1 that drops out or jumps in a way no rotating fan can, typically a loose contact in the feedback line. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's 2016 and 2018 hybrid tables, which watch the same pulse feedback, list only performance, low and high (P0BC8, P0BC9, P0BCA). Toyota's battery cooling patents show the principle: the speed measured by a rotation sensor on the fan motor is compared with the target under steady command, so a jumping signal makes that comparison worthless. CARB requires the inputs of battery thermal management to be monitored. Wiggle-test the fan connector and harness. An open line is P0BC7; fan 2 has P0D63.

causes.label: Loose or corroded terminal in the feedback circuit
Chafed harness near the fan or battery case
Intermittent fault in the fan's speed sensor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or MIL, sometimes coming and going
Fan speed reading jumping on the scan tool
Occasional power reduction

P0BCC.title: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0BCC.description: In a two-machine hybrid one inverter feeds the traction motor and a second one the generator, the machine that is mainly driven by the engine to charge the battery or start it. Its power switches carry thermistors so the controller can cut current before they overheat. P0BCC is the general circuit code for sensor A of that generator inverter, used for an electrical fault the controller does not classify as low, high or erratic. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires hybrid components and their sensor inputs to be monitored for circuit faults. Without a valid reading the controller limits generator power, which can reduce charging and hybrid performance. The sensor normally sits inside the inverter assembly.

causes.label: Fault of the sensor or its circuit inside the inverter assembly
Loose or corroded connector at the inverter
Software fault in the inverter or hybrid control module

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp
Reduced generator output and battery charging
Engine runs more often or hybrid mode limited

P0BCD.title: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0BCD.description: P0BCD flags a generator inverter temperature sensor A whose signal is electrically valid but does not fit the operating state, for example a value stuck at one temperature or far from the other temperatures after a long soak. Ford documents this exact code: on 2020 Lincoln Aviator 3.0L hybrids built up to 18 July 2020, P0BCD stored in the inverter system controller (SOBDMC) lights the MIL and is caused by software; the fix is reprogramming that module. Patents by Hino and Mitsubishi Electric describe how such checks work, comparing heat generated in the inverter with the measured temperature change or detecting a stuck sensor. Circuit faults go to P0BCE or P0BCF instead.

causes.label: Inverter controller software (Ford SSM 49120, Lincoln Aviator 2020)
Sensor drifting or stuck at one value
Uneven inverter coolant flow distorting the comparison

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp
Often no noticeable change in driving
Hybrid system warning message possible

P0BCE.title: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0BCE.description: P0BCE means the signal of generator inverter temperature sensor A is below its valid range. Inverter thermistors are usually NTC types with a pull-up resistor, as GM's tables describe for the drive motor inverter sensors: a short to ground or a shorted element pulls the voltage down, which the controller reads as an impossibly hot inverter. GM sets the comparable drive motor codes at roughly 125 to 170 °C, depending on generation. No manufacturer documents P0BCE itself publicly; CARB requires this circuit monitoring for hybrid sensor inputs. The controller then protects the generator inverter with a substitute value and limits generator power. A real overheat is reported separately as P0A3E.

causes.label: Shorted sensor or circuit inside the inverter assembly
Signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Generator power strongly limited
Battery charge drops, engine runs more

P0BCF.title: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0BCF.description: P0BCF reports a signal from generator inverter temperature sensor A above its valid range. With the usual NTC thermistor and pull-up, an open circuit, a lost sensor ground or a cracked element drives the voltage up, which reads as an extremely cold inverter. GM's comparable drive motor checks set below -40 to -58 °C and wait until the inverter has worked for about 90 s at 20 Nm or more, so a genuinely cold start does not trigger them. No manufacturer documents P0BCF itself publicly; CARB requires circuit monitoring of hybrid sensor inputs. Until the value is valid the controller uses conservative substitutes and may limit generator power. Check the inverter connectors before replacing the unit.

causes.label: Open sensor or circuit inside the inverter assembly
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the inverter
Lost sensor ground

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced generator output
Implausibly low inverter temperature in live data

P0BD0.title: Generator Inverter Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BD0.description: P0BD0 is reserved for a generator inverter temperature sensor A signal that jumps or briefly drops out instead of failing for good. A liquid-cooled inverter changes temperature slowly, so sudden steps point to a contact problem or to interference: a Hitachi patent on inverter systems explains that the small sensor signal can pick up noise from the high-voltage main circuit and has to be filtered statistically. No manufacturer documents P0BD0 itself publicly; CARB requires hybrid sensor inputs to be checked for such faults as well. Permanent faults are reported as P0BCE or P0BCF. Freeze-frame data and a wiggle test at the inverter connector help find the cause.

causes.label: Loose or corroded contact at the inverter connector
Intermittent fault inside the inverter assembly
Interference from the high-voltage circuit on the sensor signal

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief drops in generator or hybrid power
Jumping inverter temperature in live data

P0BD1.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit
P0BD1.description: Which thermistor is called sensor C depends on the maker. In GM's hybrid tables it is the second sensor of the motor A inverter: the phase V sensor in the 2016 to 2019 tables, labelled temperature sensor 2 in the Volt and ELR. P0BD1 is its general circuit code for an electrical fault that is not classified as low, high or erratic. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM reports only the specific siblings P0BD2, P0BD3 and P0BD4. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. Without a valid value the controller cannot protect that phase and normally limits motor torque. The sensor sits inside the inverter, so repairs often mean replacing the assembly.

causes.label: Internal fault of the sensor inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp
Reduced electric drive power
Possible loss of electric drive

P0BD2.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P0BD2.description: P0BD2 checks whether inverter temperature sensor C, GM's second sensor in the motor A inverter, agrees with the other temperatures after a cold soak. More than 20 °C apart sets it: Type B, two trips, on the 2016 Volt; Type A in a 2019 table; Type A on the 2011 Volt and 2016 ELR, compared with coolant and transmission temperature after 6 h off. GM's 2012 and 2013 tables use 15 °C after 360 min. GM bulletin PIC6303A says that on 2016-18 Volt, Malibu, LaCrosse and Regal the code alone needs no repair; the inverter is replaced only with P0AC4. GM fixes it by software on the 2017 Bolt EV and Ampera-e. Porsche replaces a coolant hose with a sticking thermostat on the Cayenne S E-Hybrid.

causes.label: Inverter module software (GM bulletin 18-NA-064, Bolt EV/Ampera-e)
Sticking thermostat in the power electronics coolant hose (Porsche Cayenne S E-Hybrid)
Inverter temperature sensor C drifting out of tolerance
Failing power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, often without drivability change
Propulsion power reduced message (Bolt EV)
Red hybrid warning in the cluster (Porsche)

P0BD3.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit Low
P0BD3.description: P0BD3 means the signal of inverter temperature sensor C, the phase V sensor of GM's motor A inverter, is below its valid range. GM uses an NTC thermistor with a pull-up on the sensing board, so a short to ground reads as an impossibly hot inverter. GM's thresholds: above 170 °C for 2.5 of 3.5 s, Type B, two trips, on the 2016 Volt and in a 2018 table; above 159 °C for 6.25 of 8.75 s, Type A, in a 2019 table; above 130 °C, Type A, on the 2011 Volt and 2016 ELR; above 125 °C, two trips, in the 2012 and 2013 tables. A genuine overheat of that phase is reported as P0C12. Since the sensor is part of the inverter, the usual fix is the inverter assembly.
