Sensor signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Drive motor power strongly limited
Reduced regeneration

P0BD4.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit High
P0BD4.description: P0BD4 reports a voltage from inverter temperature sensor C above its valid range. For GM's NTC sensor this is an implausibly cold inverter, typically caused by an open circuit, a lost ground or a cracked element. To avoid false alarms on a cold day GM waits until the inverter has run at least 90 s at 20 Nm or more. The 2016 Volt and a 2018 table then set it below -50 °C for 2.6 of 3.65 s, Type B, two trips; a 2019 table uses -50 °C with Type A. The 2011 Volt and 2016 ELR use below -58 °C, Type A; the 2012 and 2013 tables below -40 °C, two trips. Until the reading is valid the controller protects the inverter with substitute values and may cut motor power.

causes.label: Open sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the inverter
Lost sensor ground

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, depending on model after two trips
Reduced electric drive power
Implausibly low inverter temperature in live data

P0BD5.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BD5.description: P0BD5 is meant for an inverter temperature sensor C signal that jumps or drops out for short moments. Because the heat sink of a liquid-cooled inverter changes temperature smoothly, sudden steps point to a contact fault or to interference; a Hitachi patent explains that the small thermistor signal can pick up noise from the high-voltage main circuit. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM covers its sensor C, the phase V sensor of the motor A inverter, only with P0BD2, P0BD3 and P0BD4. CARB requires hybrid sensor inputs to be monitored for erratic faults too. Freeze-frame data and a careful check of the inverter connector are the best starting points.

causes.label: Loose or corroded contact at the inverter module
Intermittent fault inside the power inverter module
Interference from the high-voltage circuit on the sensor signal

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief power reductions while driving
Jumping inverter temperature in live data

P0BD6.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor D Circuit
P0BD6.description: Sensor D is, in GM's hybrid tables, the second thermistor of the motor B inverter, the counterpart of sensor C in the motor A inverter: phase V in the 2016 to 2019 tables, temperature sensor 2 of inverter B on the Volt. Other makers assign the letter differently. P0BD6 is its general circuit code for an electrical fault that the controller does not narrow down to low, high or erratic. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM reports P0BD7, P0BD8 and P0BD9 instead. CARB requires monitoring of hybrid sensor circuits. Without a valid value the controller cannot protect that inverter and usually limits the motor it drives. Read all stored codes, since several inverter codes often appear together.

causes.label: Internal fault of the sensor inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning or check engine lamp
Reduced electric drive or generator power
Higher fuel consumption in hybrid operation

P0BD7.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor D Circuit Range/Performance
P0BD7.description: P0BD7 is the plausibility check for inverter temperature sensor D, GM's second sensor in the motor B inverter. After a cold soak its reading is compared with an average vehicle temperature; more than 20 °C apart sets the code, Type B, two trips, on the 2016 Volt and Type A in a 2019 table. The 2011 Volt compares with power electronics coolant and transmission temperature after 6 h off (20 °C, Type A); GM's 2012 and 2013 tables use 15 °C after 360 min, two trips. GM bulletin PIC6303A lists P0BD7 with the other inverter thermistor codes on 2016-18 Volt, Malibu, LaCrosse and Regal: alone it causes no noticeable effect, and the inverter is replaced only if P0AC4 set at the same time.

causes.label: Inverter temperature sensor D drifting out of tolerance
Failing power inverter module
Uneven inverter coolant flow after soak

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, often after two trips
Often no noticeable drivability change
Further inverter temperature codes may be stored

P0BD8.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor D Circuit Low
P0BD8.description: P0BD8 means the signal of inverter temperature sensor D is below its valid range; with an NTC thermistor and pull-up that reads as an extremely hot inverter, usually from a short to ground or an internal sensor fault. GM sets it above 170 °C for 2.5 of 3.5 s, Type B, two trips, on the 2016 Volt, above 159 °C, Type A, in a 2019 table, above 130 °C, Type A, on the 2011 Volt and above 125 °C, two trips, in the 2012 table. Stellantis lists P0BD8-11 for the 2026 Jeep Compass 1.6 PHEV outside the US among the codes behind a no-start with the message Electric Traction System Fault; the repair is the traction inverter of the hybrid dual-clutch transmission.

causes.label: Shorted sensor or circuit inside the inverter (Jeep Compass PHEV bulletin)
Sensor signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where present
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Vehicle does not start, Electric Traction System Fault (Jeep)
Electric drive power strongly limited

P0BD9.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor D Circuit High
P0BD9.description: P0BD9 means inverter temperature sensor D delivers a voltage above its valid range. For GM's NTC sensor in the motor B inverter that equals an implausibly cold inverter, so an open circuit, a lost ground or a cracked thermistor is likely. GM checks only after the inverter has run at least 90 s at 20 Nm or more, so a real cold start is excluded. The 2016 Volt then sets it below -50 °C for 2.6 of 3.65 s, Type B, two trips; a 2019 table uses -50 °C with Type A; the 2011 Volt below -58 °C, Type A; the 2012 table below -40 °C, two trips. Until the value is valid the controller uses substitute values and may limit motor B. Check the inverter connectors before replacing the unit.

causes.label: Open sensor or circuit inside the power inverter module
Loose, corroded or unplugged connector at the inverter
Lost sensor ground

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp, depending on model after two trips
Reduced motor B power and regeneration
Implausibly low inverter temperature in live data

P0BDA.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BDA.description: P0BDA covers an inverter temperature sensor D signal that changes in steps or drops out briefly. Real temperatures of a liquid-cooled inverter move smoothly, so such jumps suggest a contact problem or interference from the high-voltage switching, which a Hitachi patent on inverter systems names as a typical disturbance of the small sensor signal. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's tables cover sensor D, the second sensor of the motor B inverter, only with P0BD7, P0BD8 and P0BD9. CARB requires hybrid sensor inputs to be monitored for erratic behaviour as well. Because the fault comes and goes, freeze-frame data and live data during a wiggle test are the most useful clues.

causes.label: Loose or corroded contact at the inverter module
Intermittent fault inside the power inverter module
Interference from the high-voltage circuit on the sensor signal

symptoms: Warning lamp that comes and goes
Brief power reductions while driving
Jumping inverter temperature in live data

P0BDB.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit
P0BDB.description: Which thermistor counts as inverter temperature sensor E is set by the manufacturer. In GM's hybrid tables it is the third sensor of the motor A inverter (PIM sensor #3), assigned to phase W in the 2016 to 2019 tables. P0BDB is the general circuit code for an electrical fault that is not classed as low, high or erratic. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM uses only the siblings P0BDC, P0BDD and P0BDE. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored for circuit faults. Without a valid reading the controller cannot protect the phase W power switches and usually limits motor torque. The sensor is built into the inverter, so the repair is often the inverter assembly.

causes.label: Internal fault of the thermistor or its circuit inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Reduced electric drive power
Further inverter temperature codes stored at the same time

P0BDC.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit Range/Performance
P0BDC.description: P0BDC checks whether inverter temperature sensor E, GM's phase W sensor in the motor A inverter, agrees with the vehicle after a long stand. The 2016 and 2018 tables compare it after a cold soak with a calculated average temperature; more than 20 °C apart for 0.525 of 0.625 s sets Type B, two trips. A 2019 table uses the same 20 °C as Type A. The 2011 Volt compares it with power electronics coolant temperature (20 °C, Type A); the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks use 15 °C after at least 360 minutes off (Type B). GM bulletin PIC6303A says that on 2016-18 Volt, Malibu, LaCrosse and Regal the code has no remedial action; the inverter is replaced only together with P0AC4.

causes.label: Phase W thermistor drifting out of tolerance
Uneven inverter cooling or residual heat after the soak period
Failing power inverter module (replace only with P0AC4 per GM PIC6303A)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after two drives, often without any drivability change
Code found during inspection without customer complaint

P0BDD.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit Low
P0BDD.description: P0BDD reports that the signal of inverter temperature sensor E, the phase W thermistor of GM's motor A inverter, sits below its valid range. GM uses an NTC thermistor with a pull-up on the sensing board, so a short to ground appears as an impossibly hot inverter. Thresholds: above 170 °C for 2.5 of 3.5 s, Type B, two trips, in the 2016 and 2018 tables; above 159 °C for 6.25 of 8.75 s, Type A, in a 2019 table; above 130 °C, Type A, on the 2011 Volt; above 125 °C, Type B, on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks. A real overheat of that phase is reported separately as P0C13. With the sensor inside the inverter, the usual fix is the inverter assembly.

causes.label: Shorted thermistor or signal line inside the power inverter module
Signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where the design has any
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Drive motor A power strongly limited
Reduced regenerative braking

P0BDE.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit High
P0BDE.description: P0BDE means the signal of inverter temperature sensor E is above its valid range. For GM's NTC thermistor with pull-up that reads as an extremely cold phase W in the motor A inverter, typically an open circuit, lost reference ground or a failed sensor. GM sets it below -50 °C, but only after at least 90 s of inverter warm-up at 20 Nm or more, so a genuinely cold car does not trip it: 2.625 of 3.65 s, Type B, two trips, in the 2016 and 2018 tables, 6.25 of 8.75 s, Type A, in a 2019 table. The 2011 Volt uses below -58 °C (Type A), the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks below -40 °C (Type B). The controller usually limits power to protect the unmonitored phase.

causes.label: Open thermistor or broken connection inside the power inverter module
Loose or corroded connector at the inverter
Lost sensor reference ground on the sensing board

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced electric drive power once the inverter has warmed up

P0BDF.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor E Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BDF.description: P0BDF flags an unstable signal from inverter temperature sensor E: the reading jumps or drops out briefly instead of staying out of range, typically from a loose connector, a cracked solder joint or an ageing thermistor. In GM's hybrid tables sensor E is the phase W sensor of the motor A inverter, but GM does not list this erratic code; no manufacturer documents P0BDF publicly. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be checked for circuit faults, which includes intermittent signals. Unlike P0BDD and P0BDE, the value returns to plausible levels between faults, so the code may come and go. Because the controller cannot trust the sensor, it usually reduces motor power while the fault is present.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or vibrating connector at the inverter
Cracked solder joint on the inverter sensing board
Ageing thermistor with unstable resistance

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp that comes and goes
Occasional loss of electric drive power

P0BE0.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit
P0BE0.description: Sensor F is, in GM's hybrid tables, the third thermistor of the motor B inverter (inverter B sensor #3), the counterpart of sensor E in the motor A inverter; the 2016 to 2019 tables assign it to phase W. Other makers may use the letter differently. P0BE0 is its general circuit code for an electrical fault the controller does not narrow down to low, high or erratic. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM reports P0BE1, P0BE2 and P0BE3 instead. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. Without a valid reading the controller cannot protect that inverter phase and usually limits the motor it drives. Read all stored codes, since inverter faults rarely come alone.

causes.label: Internal fault of the thermistor or its circuit inside the power inverter module
Corroded or loose connector at the inverter module
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Reduced power from drive motor B
Higher fuel consumption in hybrid operation

P0BE1.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit Range/Performance
P0BE1.description: P0BE1 is the plausibility check of inverter temperature sensor F, GM's phase W thermistor in the motor B inverter. After the car has stood long enough, its reading must match a reference: in the 2016 and 2018 tables a calculated average after cold soak, with more than 20 °C difference for 0.525 of 0.625 s setting Type B over two trips, Type A in a 2019 table. The 2011 Volt compares against power electronics coolant temperature (20 °C, Type A), the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks after 360 minutes off with a 15 °C limit (Type B). GM bulletin PIC6303A lists P0BE1 for 2016-18 Volt, Malibu, LaCrosse, Velite and Regal: no customer-noticeable reaction, inverter replacement only with P0AC4.

causes.label: Phase W thermistor of inverter B drifting out of tolerance
Uneven inverter cooling or residual heat after the soak period
Failing power inverter module (replace only with P0AC4 per GM PIC6303A)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp after two drives, usually without drivability change
Code found during inspection without customer complaint

P0BE2.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit Low
P0BE2.description: P0BE2 is set when the voltage from inverter temperature sensor F, the phase W thermistor in GM's motor B inverter, drops below the valid window. Because GM pairs an NTC element with a pull-up resistor, a short to ground is converted into a temperature far above anything the inverter can survive. Limits found in GM's tables: more than 170 °C for 2.5 of 3.5 s, Type B, two trips (2016 and 2018); more than 159 °C for 6.25 of 8.75 s, Type A (2019); more than 130 °C, Type A (2011 Volt); more than 125 °C, Type B (2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks). Genuine overheating of this phase has its own code, P0C16. The thermistor is part of the inverter, so it is rarely replaced on its own.

causes.label: Shorted thermistor or signal line inside the power inverter module
Signal shorted to ground in external wiring, where the design has any
Moisture or coolant inside the inverter housing

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Power of drive motor B strongly limited
Engine runs more often in hybrid operation

P0BE3.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit High
P0BE3.description: P0BE3 is the high-signal fault of inverter temperature sensor F, GM's phase W thermistor in the motor B inverter. With an NTC element and pull-up, an open circuit or a sensor that has lost ground drives the voltage up, which the controller reads as an implausibly cold inverter. GM only judges this after the inverter has worked for at least 90 s at 20 Nm or more: below -50 °C for 2.625 of 3.65 s sets Type B, two trips (2016 and 2018 tables), or Type A for 6.25 of 8.75 s (2019). The 2011 Volt uses below -58 °C (Type A), the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks below -40 °C (Type B). Expect limited output from motor B until the circuit is repaired.

causes.label: Open thermistor or broken connection inside the power inverter module
Loose or corroded connector at the inverter
Lost sensor reference ground on the sensing board

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B once warmed up

P0BE4.title: Drive Motor Inverter Temperature Sensor F Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0BE4.description: P0BE4 stands for brief dropouts or jumps in the signal of inverter temperature sensor F, which GM's hybrid tables place at phase W of the motor B inverter. The reading returns to normal between events, which separates it from the steady low and high faults P0BE2 and P0BE3. GM does not list this code, and no other manufacturer documents P0BE4 publicly. CARB's monitoring requirement for hybrid sensor circuits covers such intermittent faults as well. Typical sources are a connector with poor contact, a cracked solder joint or a thermistor whose resistance has become unstable. While the signal is distrusted, the controller tends to cut motor B power, and the fault can disappear before the workshop sees it.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or vibrating connector at the inverter
Cracked solder joint on the inverter sensing board
Ageing thermistor with unstable resistance

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp that comes and goes
Occasional power reduction of drive motor B

P0BE5.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Sensor Circuit
P0BE5.description: The inverter of drive motor A measures the current in each motor phase with a current sensor; the controller needs these values for torque control and overcurrent protection. P0BE5 is the general circuit code for the phase U sensor, used for an electrical fault that is not classed as offset, low or high. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's hybrid tables (2011 Volt through 2019) only use the siblings P0BE6, P0BE7 and P0BE8, and CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. Without a reliable phase U reading the inverter typically switches to a reduced or alternate control mode, so motor A loses power. The sensor sits inside the inverter, which usually means inverter replacement.

causes.label: Failed phase U current sensor inside the inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power from drive motor A
Possible loss of electric drive

P0BE6.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BE6.description: GM uses P0BE6 as the offset check of the phase U current sensor in the motor A inverter. At every start, while no current flows, the controller learns the sensor's zero offset; if it exceeds 30 A (2011 Volt and 2016 tables, Type A; 2012 two-mode trucks, Type B) or 35 A (2019 table, Type A), the code sets. In GM's BAS Plus (eAssist) table a fault of this sensor makes current control switch to an alternate mode that does not use the current sensors. Jeep lists P0BE6 with the other phase current codes on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV for Europe, with the turtle and Service 4WD lights, and fixes it by reprogramming the hybrid control processors.

causes.label: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero offset of the phase U current sensor drifted beyond the limit
Faulty sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BE7.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BE7.description: P0BE7 means the output of the phase U current sensor in the motor A inverter has fallen below its valid range. GM converts the sensor voltage into amps and compares it with a limit: below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables and 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table, both Type A; below -700 A, Type B, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; below -440 A, Type B, two trips, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table; the 2011 Volt uses 800 A limits for these sensors. Such values are far beyond real phase currents, so the cause is electrical, typically a sensor signal pulled toward ground. GM's eAssist controller then runs current control without the sensors, which costs motor A performance.

causes.label: Failed phase U current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no assist from drive motor A
Possible shutdown of electric drive

P0BE8.title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BE8.description: P0BE8 is the high-side counterpart of P0BE7: the phase U current sensor of the motor A inverter reports a value above its valid range. GM's tables set it above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), Type A, one trip; above 800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt; above 700 A, Type B, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; and above 440 A, Type B, two trips, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table. A reading this high without matching battery current points to the sensor or its supply rather than real current; genuine excess current is covered by separate overcurrent codes such as P0C01. The inverter then uses a fallback control strategy and motor A delivers less torque.

causes.label: Failed phase U current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A
Possible shutdown of electric drive

P0BE9.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit
P0BE9.description: P0BE9 covers a general circuit fault of the phase V current sensor in the motor A inverter, meaning an electrical problem the controller does not narrow down to an offset, low or high condition. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM's hybrid tables for the 2011 Volt, the 2012 two-mode trucks and the 2016 to 2019 models list only the specific siblings P0BEA, P0BEB and P0BEC; GM's BAS Plus (eAssist) table lists phase current codes only for U and W. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. Because the three phase currents are used together for torque control and their sum is cross-checked (P0BFD), a lost V signal normally forces reduced motor A operation.

causes.label: Failed phase V current sensor inside the inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BEA.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BEA.description: P0BEA is the performance check of the phase V current sensor in the motor A inverter. GM implements it as an offset test: with no current flowing at start-up, the learned zero point must stay within 30 A (2011 Volt, 2016 tables, Type A; 2012 two-mode trucks, Type B, with P0BEB/P0BEC not active) or 35 A (2019 table, Type A, after a 0.4 s delay). A sensor whose zero has drifted would distort torque control and the phase current balance. Jeep names P0BEA among the phase current codes of the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV for EMEA markets, together with the turtle and Service 4WD lights; the remedy is a software update of the hybrid control processor and power inverter.

causes.label: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero offset of the phase V current sensor drifted beyond the limit
Faulty sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BEB.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BEB.description: P0BEB reports that the phase V current sensor in the motor A inverter outputs a signal below its valid range. GM compares the converted current with a lower limit: below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016 tables) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019 table), Type A, one trip; below -800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt; below -700 A, Type B, two trips, on the 2012 two-mode trucks. Real phase currents never reach these values, so the code points to an electrical fault such as a sensor output pulled toward ground or a dead sensor. Unlike P0BEA, the sensor is not just shifted but out of its measuring range. Motor A is then run in a restricted mode.

causes.label: Failed phase V current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A
Possible shutdown of electric drive

P0BEC.title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BEC.description: P0BEC is set when the phase V current sensor of the motor A inverter reports a value above its valid range. In GM's tables the limit is above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), Type A; above 800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt with PWM output disabled; and above 700 A, Type B, two trips, on the 2012 two-mode trucks. Because the check runs while the power stage is not switching or the value is far beyond any real current, it isolates a sensor or supply fault rather than an actual overcurrent. It pairs with P0BEB for the low side and P0BEA for offset. Expect reduced drive from motor A and further inverter codes in the memory.

causes.label: Failed phase V current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BED.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit
P0BED.description: P0BED is the general circuit code of the phase W current sensor in the drive motor A inverter, for an electrical fault outside the offset, low and high categories. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's hybrid tables from the 2011 Volt to 2019, including the BAS Plus (eAssist) system, use P0BEE, P0BEF and P0BF0 instead. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. Phase W matters even on systems with only two sensors: GM's eAssist table measures U and W and, if either sensor fails, runs current control in an alternate mode without the sensors. Expect reduced motor A torque, and check for related inverter codes before replacing parts.

causes.label: Failed phase W current sensor inside the inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power or assist from drive motor A

P0BEE.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BEE.description: P0BEE checks the phase W current sensor of the motor A inverter for a plausible zero point. GM learns the sensor offset at each start while no current flows and sets the code above 30 A (2011 Volt and 2016 tables, Type A; 2012 two-mode trucks, Type B) or above 35 A (2019 table, Type A). In GM's BAS Plus (eAssist) table P0BEE is one of the faults that switch current control to a sensorless alternate mode, and it blocks the phase sum check P0BFD. Jeep lists P0BEE as Drive Motor A Inverter Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Performance on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV (EMEA), with turtle and Service 4WD lights, fixed by a hybrid control processor update.

causes.label: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero offset of the phase W current sensor drifted beyond the limit
Faulty sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BEF.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BEF.description: P0BEF indicates that the phase W current sensor of the motor A inverter delivers a signal below its valid range. GM's limits: below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016 tables) or 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), Type A; below -800 A, Type A, on the 2011 Volt; below -700 A, Type B, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; below -440 A, Type B, two trips, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table. These readings lie far outside real phase currents, so a sensor output stuck near ground, a failed sensor or a supply fault is the likely cause. In the eAssist system this fault puts current control into a mode that ignores the sensors, and it disables the U-V-W correlation check P0BFD, so motor A runs with reduced output.

causes.label: Failed phase W current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no assist from drive motor A

P0BF0.title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BF0.description: P0BF0 is the high-signal fault of the phase W current sensor in the motor A inverter. GM sets it above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table, Type A, one trip; above 700 A, Type B, two trips, on the 2012 two-mode trucks; above 440 A, Type B, in the BAS Plus (eAssist) table; the 2011 Volt uses 800 A limits for this sensor family. A value this high without matching battery current points to the sensor, its supply or an open reference rather than to real overcurrent, which GM reports separately (P0C01). With P0BF0 active, GM's eAssist logic switches to sensorless current control and suspends P0BFD, so motor A is limited until repair.

causes.label: Failed phase W current sensor inside the inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BF1.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit
P0BF1.description: On hybrids with two electric machines, the inverter of drive motor B carries its own set of phase current sensors, which the motor control processor uses for torque control and to protect the power switches. P0BF1 is the general circuit code for the phase U sensor of motor B, meant for an electrical fault that is not classified as offset, low or high. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly: GM's tables for the 2011 Volt, the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks and the 2016 to 2019 models list only P0BF2, P0BF3 and P0BF4 for this sensor. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. Without a valid phase U value, motor B is usually limited or switched off.

causes.label: Failed phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor B control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B
Engine runs more often because electric drive is limited

P0BF2.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BF2.description: GM runs P0BF2 as the offset test of the phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter. Each time the vehicle is started, while no current flows through the motor, the controller learns the sensor's zero point and compares it with a limit: 30 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A) and in the 2016 tables (Type A, after 0.1 s), 30 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, power stage open, P0BF3/P0BF4 not active) and 35 A in a 2019 table (Type A, after 0.4 s). Jeep lists P0BF2 on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV for Europe, together with the other motor A and B phase current codes, the turtle light and Service 4WD; the fix there is a software update of the hybrid control processors.

causes.label: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero point of the motor B phase U current sensor drifted past the limit
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BF3.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BF3.description: P0BF3 is stored when the phase U current sensor of the motor B inverter reports a value below its valid range. GM converts the sensor voltage into amps and sets the code below -800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, 4 of 6 samples), below -700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips), and below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip). No real phase current of motor B reaches such values, so the reading reflects an electrical defect, typically a sensor output pulled toward ground or a dead sensor. The offset check P0BF2 covers a shifted zero instead. Motor B is then restricted or shut off.

causes.label: Failed phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B
Possible shutdown of electric drive

P0BF4.title: Drive Motor B Phase U Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BF4.description: P0BF4 is the upper-limit counterpart of P0BF3 for the phase U current sensor of drive motor B. GM's thresholds: above 800 A on the 2011 Volt, checked with PWM output disabled (Type A); above 700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips); above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables and 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip). Because the test runs with the power stage idle or the value lies far beyond any real current, it points to the sensor, its supply or an open reference rather than to genuine overcurrent; GM reports real excess phase current of motor B separately under P0C04 (above 600 A in the 2016 and 2019 tables). Motor B output is limited until repair.

causes.label: Failed phase U current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B
Further inverter or phase current codes stored

P0BF5.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit
P0BF5.description: P0BF5 stands for a general circuit fault of the phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter, an electrical problem the controller does not narrow down to offset, low or high. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. GM's hybrid tables for the 2011 Volt, the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks and the 2016 to 2019 models use only the specific siblings P0BF6, P0BF7 and P0BF8; GM's single-motor BAS Plus (eAssist) system has no motor B codes at all. CARB requires circuit monitoring of hybrid sensors. Since the three phase currents of motor B are used together and their sum is cross-checked (P0BFE), losing the V signal normally forces motor B into restricted operation.

causes.label: Failed phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor B control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power from drive motor B

P0BF6.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BF6.description: P0BF6 is the performance check of the phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter, implemented by GM as a zero offset test. The offset is learned at every start with no current through the motor and must stay within 30 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, P0BEB/P0BEC not active, as printed in the table) and in the 2016 tables (Type A, 0.1 s), within 30 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips) and within 35 A in a 2019 table (Type A, 0.4 s). A shifted zero would skew torque control and the phase current balance. Jeep names P0BF6 as Drive Motor B Inverter Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV (EMEA), fixed by reflashing the hybrid control processors.

causes.label: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero point of the motor B phase V current sensor drifted past the limit
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BF7.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BF7.description: P0BF7 reports that the phase V current sensor of the motor B inverter outputs a signal below its valid range. In GM's hybrid tables the converted current must fall below -800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, one trip), below -700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, 10 of 15 samples) or below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s (2016) and 0.1 of 0.15 s (2019), both Type A. Values like these are physically impossible for the motor phase, so the controller treats them as a sensor or circuit failure, for example a shorted output or a lost sensor supply. Unlike P0BF6 the sensor is not merely offset but outside its measuring range. Drive motor B then runs restricted.

causes.label: Failed phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B
Possible shutdown of electric drive

P0BF8.title: Drive Motor B Phase V Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BF8.description: P0BF8 sets when the phase V current sensor of drive motor B reports more current than its valid range allows. GM uses above 800 A on the 2011 Volt with the PWM output disabled (Type A), above 700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips) and above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip). Such a reading while the inverter is not switching, or far above the overcurrent limit, isolates a sensor-side fault such as a signal shorted to the supply or a broken reference ground. It pairs with P0BF7 for the low side and P0BF6 for offset; real overcurrent appears as P0C04. Expect motor B to be derated and further inverter codes in memory.

causes.label: Failed phase V current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B

P0BF9.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit
P0BF9.description: P0BF9 is reserved for a general circuit fault of the phase W current sensor in the drive motor B inverter, outside the offset, low and high categories that have their own codes. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; GM's tables from the 2011 Volt through 2019, and Jeep's 2020 Renegade and Compass PHEV bulletins, refer only to the specific siblings, chiefly P0BFA. CARB requires hybrid sensor circuits to be monitored. If the controller cannot trust phase W of motor B, it can no longer close the three-phase current balance checked by P0BFE and therefore limits or disables that motor. The sensor sits inside the inverter, so repair usually means replacing the inverter assembly.

causes.label: Failed phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter
Supply or signal fault on the inverter's sensor board
Software fault in the motor B control processor

symptoms: Hybrid system warning and malfunction indicator lamp
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B

P0BFA.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0BFA.description: P0BFA checks the phase W current sensor of the motor B inverter for a plausible zero point. GM learns the offset at each start while no current flows and sets the code above 30 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, power stage open), above 30 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, only with P0BFB/P0BFC inactive), above 30 A after 0.1 s in the 2016 tables and above 35 A after 0.4 s in a 2019 table (both Type A). Jeep's EMEA bulletins for the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV put P0BFA first among the motor B codes, with MIL, turtle and Service 4WD lights, and cure it with new software for the hybrid control processor and auxiliary processor (power inverter module).

causes.label: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
Zero point of the motor B phase W current sensor drifted past the limit
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced electric drive power

P0BFB.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit Low
P0BFB.description: P0BFB indicates that the phase W current sensor of the motor B inverter delivers a signal below its valid range. GM's limits: below -800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, 4 of 6 samples at 10.4 ms), below -700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips) and below -700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A, one trip). The threshold lies well outside any phase current motor B can carry, so the likely cause is a sensor output stuck near ground, a failed sensor or a supply fault on the sensor board. P0BFA covers a shifted zero, P0BFC the high side. While the code is active, motor B delivers reduced or no torque.

causes.label: Failed phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal or supply pulled to ground on the sensor board
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power or no contribution from drive motor B

P0BFC.title: Drive Motor B Phase W Current Sensor Circuit High
P0BFC.description: P0BFC is the signal-high fault of the phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter. GM sets it above 800 A on the 2011 Volt (Type A, one trip), above 700 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type B, two trips, 10 of 15 samples) and above 700 A for 0.05 of 0.1 s in the 2016 tables or 0.1 of 0.15 s in a 2019 table (Type A). A reading this high with no matching battery current indicates the sensor, its supply or an open reference instead of actual current; true phase overcurrent of motor B is logged as P0C04, and the plausibility of all three phases together as P0BFE. With P0BFC stored the inverter derates motor B, and the hybrid system leans more on the engine and motor A.

causes.label: Failed phase W current sensor in the motor B inverter
Sensor signal shorted to the sensor supply voltage or open reference ground
Poor contact at an internal or external inverter connector

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Reduced power from drive motor B
Engine runs more often because electric drive is limited

P0BFD.title: Drive Motor A Phase U-V-W Current Sensor Correlation
P0BFD.description: In a three-phase motor without a neutral connection the three phase currents must add up to roughly zero. P0BFD checks this for drive motor A: if the absolute sum of the U, V and W readings exceeds a limit, at least one sensor is wrong. GM's limits: 156 A on the 2011 Volt and 110 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type A, one trip), 110 A for 0.0032 of 0.0038 s in the 2016 and 2019 tables (Type A). GM's BAS Plus (eAssist) uses another balance, motor DC current plus accessory module current versus battery current, above 40 A, Type B, blocked while a phase sensor code is active. Jeep lists P0BFD on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV (EMEA), fixed by a software update.

causes.label: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
One motor A phase current sensor reading wrong but still within its own limits
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced power from drive motor A

P0BFE.title: Drive Motor B Phase U-V-W Current Sensor Correlation
P0BFE.description: P0BFE applies the phase balance test to drive motor B: the controller adds the U, V and W current readings, which should cancel out, and sets the code when the absolute sum stays above a limit. GM uses 156 A on the 2011 Volt and 110 A on the 2012 and 2013 two-mode trucks (Type A, one trip, main relay closed) and 110 A for 0.0032 of 0.0038 s in the 2016 and 2019 tables (Type A). It catches a sensor that reads wrong while each signal alone stays in range, unlike the per-phase codes P0BF2 to P0BFC. GM's single-motor eAssist has no such code. Jeep lists P0BFE on the 2020 Renegade and Compass 1.3 PHEV (EMEA) with the turtle and Service 4WD lights; reprogramming the hybrid processors is the fix.

causes.label: Hybrid control processor software (Jeep bulletin 08-056-21/08-057-21)
One motor B phase current sensor reading wrong but still within its own limits
Faulty current sensing electronics in the power inverter module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp and hybrid warning
Turtle (limp home) light and Service 4WD light (Jeep)
Reduced power from drive motor B

P0BFF.title: Drive Motor A Current
P0BFF.description: P0BFF is the general code for the current flowing through drive motor A, the electric machine the manufacturer labels A. It covers a current fault that is not classed as too low (P0C00) or too high (P0C01). No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. CARB requires hybrids to monitor electric motor performance. The closest documented check is GM's P0C01, which compares the sensed phase current with a fixed limit, and Stellantis lists P0C01 on the 2026 Wagoneer S with damaged three-phase cabling as the cause. A stored P0BFF means the motor controller no longer trusts the motor current, so it usually reduces electric drive power. Check the three-phase connections, the motor windings and the inverter.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or damaged three-phase cable joint between inverter and motor A
Fault in the motor A inverter or its current measurement
Damaged stator winding of drive motor A
Motor control software fault

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp or hybrid system warning
Reduced electric drive power or limp mode
Other drive motor A current or phase codes stored
